1.title: Vision and Core Invariant
1.intent: sprag is an extensible terminal platform exposing each pane as structured cell data, not pixels, so plugins read and drive AI tools.
rationale_bullets: AI reads the screen as structured cell data, never pixels — the platform's reason to exist
Core stays closed for modification; AI-tool features attach as swappable plugins
scene-as-data is an invariant every plugin upholds, not a replaceable feature
Built on pinion as consumer and dogfood, reusing its scene-as-data RPC surface
caveats_bullets: no-pixels binds the core AND every plugin; it is the platform's purpose, not a default

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Screen-scrape a TUI multiplexer like tmux
alternatives_rejected.reason: state only visible as pixels, no extension points

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Hardcode AI loops into the core
alternatives_rejected.reason: violates open/closed; the AI ecosystem changes fast

2.title: Architecture: Core and Plugin Split
2.intent: The core owns scene-as-data consumption and the plugin extension API; AI-tool adapters, loops, and policies are swappable plugins.
rationale_bullets: Plugin extension API is the #1 core design task per README, above PTY and the cell grid
Core is the stable foundation; plugins extend it without modifying the core
The first dogfood consumer (terminal) informs the extension API; no speculative design
caveats_bullets: Extension API core is not built speculatively this iteration; the terminal slice informs it first
Statechart/codegen logic uses SCE (scxml-core-engine); pinion-forge already builds on it

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Design the extension API with no consumer

alternatives_rejected.reason: no plugin boundary; fails the platform purpose

3.title: pinion Consumer Contract
3.intent: sprag owns terminal state and projects it into pinion's GridBuffer each frame; pinion is a read-only projection, not an emulator.
rationale_bullets: pinion R969: the producer owns authoritative state; pinion projects with no per-cell mutation
Single owner of terminal state is the SSOT; GridBuffer is a one-directional derivation
Scene::TextGrid (pinion 5.41, d9f8d39) is delivered: cells, cursor, attrs, color, screen, damage
winsize SSOT: cols/rows derive from layout rect; sprag sets PTY TIOCSWINSZ from the snapshot
outputs_bullets: Per-frame GridBuffer projected into Scene::TextGrid, served over scene/snapshot
caveats_bullets: Scrollback beyond the visible screen is not modeled by pinion (R1.4 gap); the producer projects it
Glyph paint is deferred (paint-opaque); the headless data path does not need it
Headless winsize (R3): producer sets grid rect from dims x CellMetric; compute_layout is windowed
RPC server read-only (R4): scene/key does not reach the PTY; key->PTY encoding deferred (R2.6)
Winsize (R5, corrects R3): scene() leaves rect unset; authoritative dims = buffer_cols/rows
R16: scrollback is modeled producer-side via Screen::full_text (corrects the R1.4-gap above).
Screen text is single-source: in-process capture and the RPC full_text query both read full_text.

alternatives_rejected.reason: breaks producer/projection; sprag loses the state SSOT
not how TextGrid works; the buffer is replaced wholesale each frame

4.title: VT Strategy: termwiz Parser plus Owned Emulator
4.intent: Embed termwiz as the verified escape parser and cell/input primitives; sprag owns the emulator state machine behind a VtPort.
rationale_bullets: README mandate: embed a verified VT parser, do not implement it (the max-risk point)
termwiz (published, semver) supplies the verified parser, Cell/color types, and input encoding
The emulator state machine (cursor, scroll, modes, alt-screen) is sprag core IP on termwiz
VtPort isolates the VT library (open/closed) so the choice stays reversible
inputs_bullets: termwiz crate modules: escape parser, surface/cell, color, input
outputs_bullets: sprag-vt crate: VtPort trait plus a termwiz-based emulator owning screen state
caveats_bullets: termwiz gives no full emulator state machine; that layer is sprag's responsibility
Self-owned emulator reintroduces VT risk; mitigate via a conformance harness behind VtPort

alternatives_rejected.reason: effectively abandoned, fork-dependent, missing SGR attrs; fails the standard
published full emulator but API churn; less input-encoding surface
most complete but unpublished (git-rev/fork only); dependency-hygiene smell

R100.decision_summary: Round 100: consume PINION-PR47 (winit-free RPC transport-injection seam, delivered pinion R1263). Pin-bump 7 pinion-* 03e0c5a7 (R1200) to 24409c46 (R1263); SCE 3078f8bf unchanged (pinion's own SCE pin matches, one Engine instance). sprag-gui mounts an always-on fixed-path Unix-domain RPC socket (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sprag-gui.sock) through the shell's on_rpc_ingress hook, replacing the per-session stdin=FIFO wiring: the endpoint is execution-independent and the socket plus pinion's still-present stdin reader share one RpcIngress into one dispatch core (purely additive). Transport policy is sprag's (PR-47 third layer): rpc.rs owns path resolution, boot state (SPRAG_RPC), and runtime on/off via SIGUSR1 flipping TransportControl::set_enabled; the reusable UnixSocketTransport adapter is pinion-provided (pinion-rpc-transport, seam-only dep). This delivers the user ask (always-open RPC without per-session setup, plus runtime on/off) and matches the PR-47 three-layer design (dispatch=pinion, transport mechanism=reusable adapter, transport policy=consumer). Live-verified end to end.

R102.decision_summary: Round 102: fix the two smells the session review found in R100's rpc.rs. (1) The runtime on/off control was a SIGUSR1 blind toggle (set_enabled(!is_enabled())) -- not idempotent or assertable, since a lost or duplicated signal inverts the intent. Replaced with LEVEL semantics: SIGUSR1 enables, SIGUSR2 disables, so the outcome is deterministic regardless of current state (kill -USR2 always withdraws). (2) The ENDPOINT process-global was OnceLock<Arc<TransportControl>> whose doc claimed the signal thread reached the control through it -- false, the thread used its own captured Arc. Made ENDPOINT the sole owner (OnceLock<TransportControl>, no Arc): it is both the liveness anchor and where the control thread reads the control to switch exposure, so the doc is now accurate and endpoint liveness no longer depends on the control thread having spawned. Live-verified idempotency with real signals.

R103.decision_summary: Round 103: extract sprag's RPC transport policy into a new frontend-agnostic crate sprag-rpc, resolving the anticipatory duplication the session review flagged (Agent 1 #4) BEFORE the headless host gains its own socket. sprag-rpc owns the always-on Unix-socket mechanism over pinion's PR-47 RpcIngress seam: path resolution, boot state, the SIGUSR1(enable)/SIGUSR2(disable) level control, and the process-lifetime TransportControl ownership. It is GPU-free (deps: pinion-rpc + pinion-rpc-transport + signal-hook only), so both the windowed GUI and the headless host reuse it without pulling in a shell/GPU. Callers pass an Arc<dyn RpcIngress> and a SocketOpts (their socket name + env vars): the GUI's ingress comes from pinion-shell's on_rpc_ingress hook; the host's (next round) will be a channel funnel into its single dispatch owner. sprag-gui/src/rpc.rs is now a thin wrapper naming the GUI policy and delegating to sprag_rpc::mount, and sprag-gui drops its direct pinion-rpc-transport + signal-hook deps. Behavior-preserving, live-verified.

R104.decision_summary: Round 104: give the headless host (sprag-term) the always-on Unix socket, fixing the sequencing inversion the review flagged (Finding 6 -- the north-star server had only stdin while the GUI got the good transport). sprag-host now provides a single-dispatch funnel: FrameIngress (an RpcIngress that pushes frames into an mpsc channel) + dispatch_frames (the one owner thread that pulls frames and dispatches each through the existing handle_request core) + stdin_frames (the stdin producer). sprag-term mounts the socket via the shared sprag_rpc::mount with a FrameIngress, spawns the stdin producer, and runs dispatch_frames, so the socket and stdin funnel into one dispatch owner and share a consistent HostState view -- no concurrent-dispatch races, the same single-owner discipline pinion's UI thread gives the GUI. The old serve() (stdin-only, ended on EOF) is removed; the host is now a server that runs until SIGINT/SIGTERM (which cancels + joins in-flight plugin runs so a slow AI turn reaps). GPU-free throughout. Live-verified with stdin=/dev/null: the socket serves the full platform (panes+mux+plugins), SIGUSR1/2 toggle it idempotently, SIGTERM exits cleanly.

R105.decision_summary: Round 105: begin the GUI-as-client-of-host increment. Topology DECIDED (user, cost-no-object "most long-term-correct"): B -- the GUI is a PURE transport-abstracted WIRE CLIENT of the host (tmux/mosh pattern; the read-data-not-pixels invariant becomes STRUCTURAL, not a shared-Arc convention; enables multi/remote/alt-frontend clients + fault isolation). This round is the topology-neutral first step of the prescribed sequence (unify scene-assembly SSOT -> host owns Workspace -> GUI attaches): decouple the pane-node ASSEMBLY from live-Screen PROJECTION. New pub pane_view_scene_from_cells(tag, cells, metric, font_size_px) is the Screen-free pane-node SSOT (focus-stop Container + composite {tag}#grid click anchor + R1002 font pin) that assembles the node from an already-projected GridBuffer alone; pane_view_scene(tag, spec) is now a thin live-Screen convenience over it (project_scrolled + overlay_preedit, then delegate), signature unchanged so the in-process GUI caller (build_pane_scene) is untouched. This is the exact seam the future wire client shares -- it will feed cells reconstructed off the host's served data model to build the byte-identical pane node without ever touching a live Screen. Behavior-preserving.

R107.decision_summary: Round 107: increment 2, step 1 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = PROVE the wire-fidelity assumption before any wiring (test-the-risky-assumption-first). New sprag-host test wire_round_trip_preserves_the_pane_cell_buffer establishes topology B's load-bearing guarantee: the paint-authoritative pinion GridBuffer (serde-able since PR-49/R106) survives a serde_json round-trip byte-for-byte on REAL projected production data -- indexed + truecolor + default colours, bold + reverse attrs, a wide (CJK) head+trailer cluster, the cursor (position/shape/visibility), the Alternate screen kind, and per-row damage generations. It asserts the whole buffer is Eq after round-trip (the strongest claim), plus position-independent per-field spot-checks so a dropped field names itself, plus that the CLIENT node assembled from the round-tripped buffer (pane_view_scene_from_cells, the R105 seam) carries the same cells as the direct projection -- i.e. a wire display client paints identically to the host. If serde ever drops a field the human/GUI path would render differently from the host's served data and the read-data-not-pixels invariant would break silently in the GUI; this fails HERE, in the crate that owns the wire seam, instead. Pure test addition: zero production change, zero render risk. Next (R108): the actual wiring -- host pane_cells data query + GUI reroute through pane_cells + client-side overlay_preedit + pane_view_scene_from_cells + removal of the now-superseded pane_view_scene/PaneViewSpec, live A/B-verified.

R108.decision_summary: Round 108: increment 2 wiring of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc -- the GUI now consumes the host's per-pane cell DATA query as a client (in-process), replacing the all-in-one pane builder. New pub sprag_host::pane_cells(session, offset_lines) -> GridBuffer is the named host data-query surface (the projection half of the old builder); sprag-gui build_pane_scene reroutes to pane_cells (host data) + sprag_grid::overlay_preedit (CLIENT-local IME overlay, an uncommitted composition never in the PTY) + pane_view_scene_from_cells (CLIENT Screen-free assembly) -- the three steps that split along the wire boundary in increment 3. R109.decision_summary: Round 109: increment 3 round 1 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = the in-process CLIENT SEAM. Introduced sprag-gui/src/host.rs LocalHost: the GUI now reaches its panes ONLY through a typed client protocol (pane_count, pane_cells, pane_dims, pane_pty_size, pane_id, resize, pane_handle, pane_full_text, pane_command_label), encapsulating the single Workspace it owns. TerminalView changed from a public workspace: Workspace field (reached into directly across the GUI) to host: LocalHost (Workspace private) + the client's own rendering config (metric, font_size_px -- deliberately NOT host state). Rerouted all ~8 production coupling sites across 6 files (view build_pane_scene -> pane_cells + pane_dims; reflow -> pane_pty_size + resize; a11y pane_node -> pane_full_text + pane_command_label; dock undock size -> pane_pty_size; main create_external(s) -> pane_handle + reconcile_frame -> pane_dims; input scroll_view -> pane_dims, cycle_focus -> pane_count) plus the test call sites. The Workspace still lives in the GUI process (behind LocalHost) so this is behaviour-preserving and reversible; it is the exact method surface a wire transport backs in the later transport step, WITHOUT the call sites changing. Per the user's cost-no-object decision, this validates the client protocol against a real in-process consumer FIRST; the HostClient trait is extracted when the wire adds the second consumer (an interface designed against two impls is more correct than one). Input still flows through pane_handle/SpragPaneExternal (round 2 moves it over the client); the single-owner unification + wire transport land in later rounds.

R110.decision_summary: Round 110: increment 3 round 2 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = INPUT over the client. The GUI's keyboard + IME-commit now go through the host client (LocalHost::send_key/send_text) instead of finding+invoking the pane's SpragPaneExternal in its own paint scene -- topology B: the GUI's input is a client SEND, not a mutation of its own scene (over the wire it becomes an RPC to the host; the GUI's scene will not hold the host's externals). Extracted the key->PTY encode+write SSOT into sprag_host::send_key/send_text (shared by the RPC input surface SpragPaneExternal::invoke AND the in-process client), so the human keyboard path and the AI scene/invoke path encode IDENTICALLY. LocalHost gained send_key(index, key, Modifiers) / send_text(index, text); route_key/route_composition drop their &mut Scene param (input no longer reads the paint scene) and call use_terminal().host.send_key/send_text; apply_key/apply_key_repeat/apply_composition (the WidgetCore trait methods) keep the trait-required scene param as _scene and pass nothing to the route fns. Added sprag-input as a direct sprag-gui dep (the Modifiers type + the meta->sup conversion to_input_mods). The pane input SpragPaneExternals STAY registered in the GUI's model scene (its RPC input surface); removing them is a later step. Behaviour-preserving (same encode+write SSOT). Reworked the 2 scene-inject tests into deterministic LocalHost tests + a focus-gate test; the chord tests are unaffected.

R111.decision_summary: Round 111: adversarial session review of the R105-R110 GUI-as-client-of-host arc (3 independent lenses -- architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell, correctness/behaviour -- run in parallel, every finding cross-checked against the actual code before acting), then remediation. VERDICT: the load-bearing structure + SSOT are at the textbook bar (send_key/send_text single encoder SSOT shared by the RPC SpragPaneExternal AND the client; grid_node kernel; pane_cells/overlay/assemble split; runtime encapsulation verifiably enforced -- no GUI path touches Workspace/session outside host.rs) and NO reroute changed behaviour (all delegations byte-identical old-vs-new; the suspected TOCTOU is the pre-existing two-lock gap unchanged, the modifier mapping and empty-commit guard are identical). The real gaps were doc-honesty + test-coverage that slipped from moving fast -- exactly what the review exists to catch. Remediated ALL: (A) host.rs module header still said input flows through the SessionHandle post-R110 -> rewrote to enumerate send_key/send_text as protocol + honestly scope pane_handle as the one non-wire method + dual-authority/retirement transitional notes; (B) stale pane_view_scene name in the sprag-host pane_grid test helper (a dangling intra-doc link hidden in cfg(test)) -> pane_view_scene_from_cells; (C) route_composition non-empty Commit->send_text was covered by NO test -> restored an end-to-end apply_composition Commit test; (D) route_key multi-pane inject-through-apply_key untested -> restored an end-to-end apply_key routing test; both via a new #[cfg(test)] terminal::seed_terminal seam (deterministic cat panes, not shell-echo); (E) LocalHost::pane_id was pub protocol but only self-called -> private; (F) LocalHost::send_key/send_text dropped the host SSOT #[must_use] hiding route_composition discarded write -> #[must_use] + explicit let _ with rationale; (G) PaneDims/pane_dims -> PaneScrollFacts/pane_scroll_facts (scrollback_len is a depth, not a dimension); (J) pane_pty_size -> pane_grid_size (reads the emulator, not the PTY winsize); (K) resize swallowed error now traced; (N) trimmed a two-frontends-share plurality overclaim; plus removed the inert Scene::External boilerplate from the chord tests. Deferred (documented, YAGNI/round-3): LocalHost::pane -> Option when close lands; LocalHost owning spawn (needs the RepaintSink injected -- round-3 host unification); a combined pane_frame query. Behaviour-preserving; live-verified.

R112.decision_summary: Round 112: increment 3 round 3 of the GUI-as-client-of-host arc = the Workspace-ownership flip into ONE shared host component. Moved the single Workspace owner + typed client protocol out of the GUI (sprag-gui/src/host.rs LocalHost, deleted) into sprag-host as pub Host: it owns Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> (the shape the headless HostState and the topology-B end state already use), boots panes via spawn(command,label,cols,rows,on_dirty) taking an optional pinion-free Box<dyn Fn()+Send> wake hook (the GUI passes the RepaintSink closure, the headless server passes None), and serves the same protocol LocalHost did (pane_count/pane_cells/pane_scroll_facts/pane_grid_size/resize/send_key/send_text/pane_full_text/pane_command_label/pane_handle). Both frontends now boot through this ONE component: the GUI holds a Host in-process (TerminalView.host: Host; every ~30 pane call site across view/reflow/a11y/dock/main/input is UNCHANGED thanks to the R109 seam), and sprag-term boots its initial pane through the same Host, now wrapped by HostState (which holds a Host, not a raw Arc, and delegates workspace()). PaneScrollFacts moved to sprag-host; pane_command_label returns an owned String (the workspace lock is released before it returns); resize resolves index to PaneId under one lock; with_pane centralises the lock+lookup. Per the R109 cost-no-object decision the HostClient trait stays deferred to round 4 (the wire step, where a 2nd impl validates the interface). Behaviour-preserving; no pinion change needed (spawn_with_dirty was already pinion-free).

R114.decision_summary: Round 114: pin-bump pinion 950f73ef(R1266) -> 33e2ebcf(R1271) to CONSUME PINION-PR50 (async scene/waitFor), the topology-B round-4 (wire transport) repaint-over-wire blocker. pinion delivered it across R1269 (feat: async scene/waitFor via a park/wake registry -- new crates/pinion-rpc/src/waiter.rs WaiterRegistry that parks the RpcReply keyed by `since` and is woken off the one SceneRevision, plus the pinion-shell wiring + hello-live-data reference consumer) and R1270 (audit-clearance: pinion-core SceneRevision::set_observer wake-observer hook, condvar no-lost-wakeup discipline, dispatch/methods integration). This is exactly the PR-50 shape sprag requested: dispatch deferred-reply (park + fire off-dispatch) + external-data-arrival wakeup (the host's on_dirty advances the revision and wakes parked waiters), the section 6.3 async boundary the wait_for v0 doc named. Enabling bump only: sprag code change 0 -- the wire client that CONSUMES try_async_wait_for is a later round (R115, the actual round-4 wire work, confirm before it). SCE unchanged (pinion@33e2ebcf pins SCE 3078f8bf = sprag's current pin -> the single shared Engine<StatePolicy> instance is preserved, no SCE bump). The bump also picks up the intervening R1267 (tray SNI CI fixture) + R1268/R1271 (pinion-text auto-indent + Enter undo boundary) which are tray / text-editor-domain, orthogonal to sprag's terminal/dock/shell usage.

R115a.decision_summary: Round 115a: the headless host serves the async change-notification contract (PR-50 consumed) -- increment 3 round 4 (WIRE transport) sub-step 1, additive, in-process GUI untouched. A wire client repaints on a pane's output by blocking on scene/waitFor instead of busy-polling scene/snapshot; this round makes sprag-term serve exactly that. HostState now holds a shared Arc<SceneRevision> (the ONE scene-version token, shared with the pane on_dirty bumpers) + an Arc<WaiterRegistry>, and installs the wake observer in new() (revision.set_observer(move |n| waiters.wake(n))). dispatch_frames is split into a per-frame dispatch_one that intercepts an async scene/waitFor {since} through pinion's try_async_wait_for BEFORE the synchronous handle_request: it parks the RpcReply (fires later, off the dispatch thread, on the scene bump that wakes it) or answers immediately if the scene already advanced; a non-waitFor / since-less frame hands the reply back for normal dispatch, so parking never builds the workspace scene. scene/revision + scene/waitFor added to SUPPORTED_METHODS (scene/revision is pinion's non-blocking read the client bootstraps its `since` from). sprag-term boot creates the revision BEFORE spawning and wires the initial pane's on_dirty to bump it, so the pane's output wakes parked waiters. This is the wake half only; serving pane cells as GridBuffer over the wire (R115b) and the GUI wire client + irreversible cutover (R115c) are later sub-steps. No pinion change (consumes R1269/R1270 WaiterRegistry/try_async_wait_for/SceneRevision::set_observer, delivered + bumped R114).
changes_bullets: sprag-host/rpc.rs: HostState gains revision: Arc<SceneRevision> (was owned SceneRevision) + waiters: Arc<WaiterRegistry>; HostState::new(host, revision) installs revision.set_observer(move |n| waiters.wake(n)); accessors revision()/waiters(); handle_request's DispatchContext uses state.revision(). SUPPORTED_METHODS += scene/revision, scene/waitFor. method_not_supported message names the full set.

sprag-host/rpc.rs: dispatch_frames split into per-frame dispatch_one(state, frame) -- parse_request then try_async_wait_for(&parsed, state.revision(), state.waiters(), reply): ControlFlow::Break => parked (return, reply fires later on wake), Continue(reply) => normal handle_request; malformed hands the reply back to handle_request's parse-error path.

R115b.decision_summary: Round 115b: the headless host serves pane cells as a GridBuffer FRAME over RPC -- increment 3 round 4 (WIRE transport) sub-step 2, additive, in-process GUI untouched. This is the wire display client's per-frame DATA read (topology B): SpragPaneExternal gains a read-shaped `cells` invoke action -- invoke("cells", {offset}) -> IntrospectValue::Json({cells: <GridBuffer>, scrollback_len, visible_rows}). It is an invoke rather than a query because it carries the `offset` scrollback parameter, which pinion's path-only scene/query cannot (the open design point of R115b, settled: invoke is the only RPC method that carries args and returns a value). The three fields are read under ONE screen lock -- an atomically consistent snapshot (cells + scroll facts describe the same screen state, no torn read across two locks, unlike the in-process Host which takes pane_cells + pane_scroll_facts as two separate locks) -- and the GridBuffer is serialized AFTER the lock is released, so the CPU-bound serialization never holds the producer's screen. offset==0 is the live view; a larger offset windows into history (sprag_grid::project_scrolled self-clamps to the retained depth). The GridBuffer is serde-able since PINION-PR49, so the client reconstructs the EXACT buffer the host projected and feeds it to pane_view_scene_from_cells (the R105 client-assembly seam) to paint byte-for-byte -- "read data, not pixels" reaches the human path. Additive: the in-process GUI reads cells via Host::pane_cells directly (never this action); only the wire client (R115c) uses it. No pinion change.
changes_bullets: sprag-host/pane.rs: SpragPaneExternal gains a `cells` invoke action (CELLS_ACTION). read_cells(args) parses the scrollback offset, projects the scrolled GridBuffer + reads scrollback_len/visible_rows under ONE screen lock, then (off the lock) serializes to Json({cells, scrollback_len, visible_rows}). parse_offset_arg accepts null/absent (->0 live), a bare non-negative int, or {offset:N}; a negative/non-integer offset is TypeMismatch (project_scrolled self-clamps over-large offsets). CELLS_ACTION added to schema + the invoke match. Module doc documents the read-shaped invoke + why-invoke-not-query. Imports serde_json::json; calls sprag_grid::project_scrolled (both already deps of sprag-host).

Tests: +1 pane.rs unit (parse_offset_defaults_to_live_and_rejects_negatives). +2 rpc.rs integration over the full dispatch path: pane_cells_action_returns_a_deserializable_grid_frame (the cells JSON deserializes back into the exact GridBuffer, dims + "hi" content, scroll facts present) and pane_cells_action_honors_the_scrollback_offset (40 lines / 4 rows: scrollback_len>0, and a scrolled buffer != the live buffer). cells_frame test helper.

R115c.decision_summary:
Round 115c: the GUI becomes a pure wire client of a sprag-term host PROCESS (topology B, the round-4 wire step; user-confirmed B+na -- spawn-or-attach, wire is the GUI default). The single Workspace/PTY owner now lives in a separate process and the GUI owns none of it. Extracted the host's typed surface into pub trait HostClient (pane_count / pane_cells / pane_scroll_facts / pane_grid_size / resize / send_key / send_text / pane_full_text / pane_command_label) with two impls: the in-process Host and a new WireHost. TerminalView.host became Box<dyn HostClient>, so the ~30 GUI pane call sites are byte-identical across the two impls -- the R109 seam paying off across the process boundary. pane_handle left the trait (a live SessionHandle cannot cross a wire) and the GUI's own per-pane SpragPaneExternal input surface retired: input is now a client SEND to the host (keyboard via HostClient::send_key; an AI peer drives the host socket directly), and the primary external is pane 0's scrollbar.

Added a blocking JSON-RPC HostConn client to sprag-rpc (connect-with-readiness-retry + call), the client twin of the existing server mount. WireHost spawns a sprag-term child (per-pid socket, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG + kill-on-Drop) or attaches to SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK, boots n_panes over the sprag_mux spawn, maps tile index to PaneId, and runs a background poll thread that parks on the async scene/waitFor change-notification, refetches every pane's live cells into a shared cache, and calls request_repaint -- the off-thread-producer to repaint shape hello-live-data proves. view reads the cache (never a blocking socket call on the paint path); a scrolled-history read (offset > 0) is the one synchronous fetch. pane_grid_size reads GUI-tracked dims (the GUI is the resize authority) so the reflow guard sees a resize immediately with no round-trip and no resize loop. No pinion change (the client is a sprag concern; PINION-PR50 already cleared the repaint-over-wire blocker). Unit tests default to the in-process Host (a test cannot spawn a real child); production defaults to wire; SPRAG_GUI_HOST=inprocess is the escape hatch.

Exported from lib.rs; two pane.rs intra-doc links repointed to HostClient.

R116.decision_summary:
Round 116: adversarial 3-lens session review of R112-R115b (the GUI-as-client-of-host / round-4 wire work) + remediation, at the user's cost-no-object textbook bar. Three independent lenses ran in parallel (architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell, correctness/concurrency); every finding was cross-checked against the actual code before acting (the R111 discipline). VERDICT: structure is long-term-correct toward topology B, the concurrency is sound (no bug/deadlock/reachable panic -- the correctness lens confirmed no-lost-wakeup, one-directional WORKSPACE->SCREEN lock order, wake-outside-lock, and read_cells' atomic snapshot against pinion's WaiterRegistry/SceneRevision source), and NOTHING was given up for cost -- EXCEPT one real SSOT blemish R115b introduced by hand-writing the wire frame's JSON instead of reusing the typed facts. Remediated all real findings; two were deliberately deferred to R115c with explicit rationale (not skipped for convenience). This changed CODE STRUCTURE only -- the wire JSON contract and all behaviour are byte-identical (re-verified live over the real socket).

Fixed: (SSOT, both lenses) the pane cell-frame's non-cell field set was defined twice -- the typed PaneScrollFacts struct AND a hand-built json! literal in SpragPaneExternal::read_cells -> now ONE type: PaneScrollFacts gains serde derive + a single from_screen population site, and read_cells serializes a CellFrame that #[serde(flatten)]s PaneScrollFacts, so the field names ARE the wire keys and the population is single-sourced. (silent-failure guard, correctness lens) HostState::new discarded SceneRevision::set_observer's install-once bool -> a future revision-reuse would hang every waitFor with no error; now assert!ed. (DRY, both lenses) dispatch_one parsed then handle_request re-parsed every frame -> extracted a handle_parsed core that dispatch_one calls with the already-parsed Request (parse-once on the hot path); handle_request stays the string entry for tests + the malformed path. (SSOT) method_not_supported hand-listed the methods SUPPORTED_METHODS already defines -> SUPPORTED_METHODS.join. (SSOT/invariant) the "spawn a pane whose output bumps THIS revision" boot recipe was hand-wired in sprag-term.rs AND the test -> one pub bump_on_dirty(&revision) helper both use. (doc-honesty) two stale LocalHost references the R112 comment-sweep missed (pane.rs send_key pub doc + sprag-gui/Cargo.toml) -> Host::send_key. (cleanup) a dead handle binding in a host test. Deferred to R115c (documented): the per-pane cells action vs the workspace-level waitFor granularity (the "batch is the natural wire shape" call, made when the wire client is built); and collapsing the in-process GUI's 2-lock cells+facts read to the wire path's 1-lock atomic frame (the GUI's offset math needs scrollback_len first -- it resolves structurally when the GUI becomes a wire client). No pinion change; no behaviour change.
changes_bullets: SSOT frame unification: PaneScrollFacts (host.rs) gains #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] + a pub(crate) from_screen(screen) single population site; Host::pane_scroll_facts calls from_screen. pane.rs read_cells builds a CellFrame { cells: GridBuffer, #[serde(flatten)] facts: PaneScrollFacts } via from_screen under one lock and serializes it -- the wire keys {cells, scrollback_len, visible_rows} now come from the types, not a hand-built json! literal. Removed the now-unused top-level serde_json::json import from pane.rs; added pinion_core::GridBuffer + crate::host::PaneScrollFacts imports.

rpc.rs: HostState::new asserts revision.set_observer(...) returned true (install-once silent-failure guard). Extracted pub handle_parsed(state, Request) as the dispatch core; handle_request(state, &str) parses then delegates (string entry + malformed parse-error path); dispatch_one parses once and calls handle_parsed with the parsed Request on the non-waitFor path (no re-parse). method_not_supported uses SUPPORTED_METHODS.join(", "). New pub bump_on_dirty(&Arc<SceneRevision>) -> Box<dyn Fn()+Send> helper (the pane on_dirty->revision.bump recipe); exported from lib.rs alongside handle_parsed.
sprag-term.rs boot + the rpc.rs host_with test helper both use bump_on_dirty (one recipe, prod == test). host.rs test send_text_reaches_the_pane_pty dropped a dead pane_handle binding.

Deps: added serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] } to the workspace + sprag-host (matches pinion's serde; the one instance is shared). Stale LocalHost -> Host in pane.rs send_key doc + sprag-gui/Cargo.toml comment.
verification_bullets: Review method: 3 adversarial lenses (architecture/SSOT, refactoring/smell, correctness/concurrency) ran in parallel; every finding cross-checked against the actual code before acting (2-of-N candidate concerns from my own pre-read were confirmed real; the concurrency lens found NO live bug -- it verified the park/wake, lock order, and atomic-snapshot against pinion's waiter.rs/revision.rs source). No finding was manufactured; the deferred items carry explicit rationale.

cargo test --workspace 241 passed / 0 failed (unchanged count -- pure refactor + one dead-binding removal); clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps clean (fixed 3 now-redundant GridBuffer explicit link targets + a public->private dispatch_one link introduced by the refactor); rustfmt clean.

Behaviour-preserving, RE-VERIFIED LIVE over the real sprag-term socket after the refactor: (1) R115a async scene/waitFor still parks then wakes on a pane's output (parked -> injected pane output on a 3rd connection -> woke at revision 2); (2) R115b cells frame keys are byte-identical {cells, scrollback_len, visible_rows} with the GridBuffer nested (serde flatten produces the same wire shape as the old hand-built json); (3) scene/query works and method-not-found now lists the SUPPORTED_METHODS-derived set including scene/waitFor. The wire JSON contract did not change -- only the code that produces it.
carry_forward_bullets: R116 = adversarial 3-lens review of R112-R115b + remediation. VERDICT: topology-B structure is long-term-correct, SSOT holds (after this fix), concurrency sound, nothing given up for cost. All real findings fixed; wire contract byte-identical (behaviour-preserving).

The frame SSOT is now: PaneScrollFacts (serde, one from_screen population) is the ONE non-cell field-set; the wire CellFrame flattens it; the in-process Host::pane_scroll_facts reads it. handle_parsed is the dispatch core (parse-once); bump_on_dirty is the one pane-output->revision-bump recipe.

DEFERRED to R115c (documented, NOT skipped for convenience): (a) per-pane cells action vs workspace-level waitFor -- decide batch-vs-per-pane when the wire client is built (a woken client re-queries which pane? -- a workspace batch may be the natural shape given one revision for the whole scene). (b) the in-process GUI reads cells+facts under 2 locks (torn read, self-corrects next frame, single-threaded-safe -- confirmed not a live bug) while the wire path is 1-lock atomic; unify when the GUI becomes a wire client (its offset math needs scrollback_len first, so a single atomic frame is natural only once the GUI long-polls).

NEXT is still R115c (the GUI wire client, IRREVERSIBLE -- confirm before): HostClient trait (2 impls: in-process Host + socket client), GUI spawns/attaches a host process, try_async_wait_for long-poll -> request_repaint -> re-query the cells frame, retire pane_handle + the GUI's own SpragPaneExternal. The host now serves the full wire contract (change-notification + cells frame + input + pane list/plugins). serde is now a workspace dep (derive) for sprag's wire DTOs.

Round 10.decision_summary: Extract the plugin extension API (the README #1 concern) from two real consumers: PaneAccess (data API) + a Plugin/Driver behavior-vs-substrate split, validated by the orchestrator plus a new pipe plugin.
changes_bullets: Renamed sprag-orchestrator -> sprag-plugin; it is now the plugin substrate, split into modules: access (PaneAccess + WorkspacePaneAccess + KeyStroke/PaneRow/InjectError), plugin (Plugin::step + Step + Verdict), driver (Driver + Guardrails + Outcome/OutcomeState), and the bundled orchestrator + pipe plugins. Pinion-free.

PaneAccess is the extension API: pane_ids / pane_collapsed / pane_rows (generation+text in one locked snapshot, killing a TOCTOU race) / inject (returns bytes). WorkspacePaneAccess over Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> is the single read+inject path, so plugins stop reaching into SessionHandle directly (review finding D, read-path unification).

Split the orchestrator loop: the Driver owns the SCE statechart (flattened to idle->running->{converged,exhausted,failed}) plus the guardrails (max_iterations/max_injected_bytes moved off OrchestrationSpec onto Guardrails); Plugin::step owns perceive/act/judge. The orchestrator (fixed-stimulus drive) and a new Pipe (relay a source pane's newly-damaged rows into a destination pane; never self-converges, guardrails bind) both impl Plugin.

The Pipe is the second consumer that proves the abstraction generalizes: same damage-generation primitive as the orchestrator's observe, but a plugin-owned cursor (after-last-relay vs before-last-stimulus). act/judge were collapsed into one step (so the statechart's internal phases do not leak into the plugin contract); inject returns the byte count feeding the Driver's cost guardrail.
verification_bullets: 59 workspace tests pass. The orchestrator's four tests pass unchanged in intent via Driver::run(&mut Orchestrator, panes) -- the regression gate proving the extraction preserved behavior; plus two WorkspacePaneAccess tests and the pipe proof test (seed source, relay into destination, exhaust on the iteration budget). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

The design was pressure-tested by a Plan agent that corrected five points before implementation: a single step (not act/judge), pane_rows folding text+generations to remove a TOCTOU race, inject returning the byte count, the flattened statechart, and deferring the host-External base to the exposure round.

Crate rename was contained (nothing depended on sprag-orchestrator yet); build stayed green at each phase. SCE needed nothing new (same usage as Round 8); pinion's vendored SCE remained content-identical to canonical.
carry_forward_bullets: Exposure round: OrchestratorExternal / a plugin host over RPC -- start/observe a Driver::run off the serve thread (background execution), so external AI peers drive plugins as scene-as-data -- and extract the shared host-External base (backends/repaint/thread_ownership/Debug/arg-parse) from the now three Externals at that point.

AI-tool adapters (claude/aider in panes with structured I/O) + bidirectional A<->B relay + character-level delta diffing (the pipe relays whole rows on a generation bump today) are the real AI<->AI layer beyond this substrate.
PaneAccess additions (cell/style read, scrollback) stay additive until a consumer needs them (YAGNI).

Round 11.decision_summary: Expose plugins over RPC, completing the plugin-platform contract: a PluginsExternal runs plugins on background threads (non-blocking serve) tracked in a shared RunRegistry, plus the shared host-External boilerplate extraction.
changes_bullets: New PluginsExternal (sprag-host): scene/invoke run (a plugin discriminator orchestrator|pipe, submit-time pane validation -> synchronous Rejected, DEFAULT_GUARDRAILS, spawns a background Driver::run that writes the terminal RunState) + scene/query runs/plugins; the plugin Outcome is rendered to JSON in the host so sprag-plugin stays serde-free. Added as the sprag_plugins child of workspace_scene.

Run registry: the long-lived state is a shared Arc<Mutex<RunRegistry>> owned by serve and threaded via a HostState{workspace,runs,previews,revision} bundle -- NOT owned by the per-request PluginsExternal, which is a throwaway projection rebuilt each request (the critical bug a Plan agent caught). Each run carries its own Arc<Mutex<RunState>> cell so reading the registry never blocks behind a run; sweep joins finished threads (is_finished, non-blocking; a panic becomes Panicked); join_all on RunRegistry Drop and serve shutdown reaps threads (bounded by guardrails).

E-extraction: a sprag-host-local rpc_external_impl! macro (mirroring pinion's query_proxy_external_impl!, but &[Rpc]-only) plus a shared lock and arg helpers (as_object/require_pane_id/require_str/opt_str/opt_dim) in a new external module; SpragPaneExternal and WorkspaceExternal rewritten onto them (each keeps its own ExternalIntrospect and Debug).

Producer correctness: Workspace::close now returns the removed Pane so the caller drops it (TerminalSession::drop's kill/wait/join) OUTSIDE the workspace lock, so a close can no longer stall an in-flight plugin run contending on that lock.
verification_bullets: 64 workspace tests pass: a background converged run over RPC (poll query(runs) to done), a synchronous Rejected for an unknown target pane, a non-blocking responsiveness test (a sleep pane's slow run does not delay an immediate snapshot), a Driver Err->Failed unit test via a mock PaneAccess (no threads), the registry submit/sweep/join lifecycle, and the existing host/producer suites. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

Bin end-to-end (sprag-term -- cat): scene/invoke /sprag_plugins/external/run returns a run id; scene/query plugins returns [orchestrator, pipe]; query runs shows the run reaching done with outcome converged (iterations 1, injected_bytes 5).

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent which caught the registry-ownership bug and refined the reaping (is_finished join), shutdown (join_all on Drop), and guardrail-default model. pinion/SCE needed nothing new.
carry_forward_bullets: Interactive cancel (designed, deferred): an Arc<AtomicBool> trigger checked atop Driver::run's loop firing a cancel event to a new cancelled statechart final + OutcomeState::Cancelled -- the terminal state stays in the chart (SCE dogfood), the flag is only the trigger. Without it, host shutdown blocks until in-flight runs finish (the honest cost).
AI-tool adapters (claude/aider in panes with structured I/O) as the real AI<->AI plugins over this exposed substrate; bidirectional A<->B relay; character-level delta diffing for the pipe.
Live per-iteration run progress and run GC from the registry are deferred until a consumer needs them (YAGNI; Outcome already carries iterations/injected_bytes).

Round 12.decision_summary: First AI-tool adapter: an Agent plugin runs a real AI CLI (claude -p) in a pane, drives it via injected keystrokes, and captures its reply as structured output surfaced over RPC — converging on child-exit.
changes_bullets: New crate file crates/sprag-plugin/src/agent.rs: the one-shot Agent plugin (AgentSpec{prompt, eof, timeout}). step() injects prompt + Enter + (Ctrl-D/EOF if eof) via the R6 sprag-input encoder, waits for the pane child to finish, then captures the damaged-row delta since the prompt as the reply. Pinion-free.

Completion via child-exit, not output quiescence: new PaneAccess::pane_eof (WorkspacePaneAccess reads TerminalSession::is_eof under the workspace lock; NO sprag-terminal change, is_eof was already public via Pane::session()). is_eof's 'all bytes applied once EOF observed' contract makes the capture race-free and defeats the prompt-echo/think-time race a debounce would hit (the injected prompt echoes back before the model starts replying).

New content seam: Plugin::captured() default-None trait method — the Driver stays content-agnostic; the host worker reads plugin.captured() after Driver::run (it still owns the plugin) and stores it. RunState::Done became a struct variant {outcome, output: Option<String>}; run_to_json renders the captured reply as the run's 'output'.

Host wiring (sprag-host/plugins.rs): PluginsExternal 'agent' run arm (require pane + prompt; optional eof/timeout_ms), BoxedPlugin::Agent variant, PLUGINS gains 'agent'. No new pinion RPC methods and no new SCXML states/events — the Agent maps to Verdict::Converged after one step on the existing idle->running->converged statechart.
verification_bullets: 68 workspace tests pass (+4): agent.rs converges_and_captures_a_reply and captures_a_complete_multiline_reply (real PTY + a deterministic read-until-EOF fake-AI shell fixture, sh -c 'in=$(cat); echo REPLY[$in]'); rpc.rs runs_an_agent_plugin_to_done_capturing_its_reply (background run over the dispatch path, reply surfaced as the run's output) and lists_the_agent_among_available_plugins. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

Genuine AI<->AI verified manually: the #[ignore]d agent::tests::drives_real_claude spawns a real 'claude -p' pane, injects the prompt via the encoder, and captures 'PONG' (cargo test -- --ignored, passed in ~1.2s). Gated #[ignore] because it needs the claude CLI + network + auth and is non-deterministic; offline coverage is the fake-AI fixture.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: confirmed NO pinion/SCE change is needed (stop-and-report clean), validated the captured()/RunState ripple and the worker-still-owns-plugin-after-run ownership, and flagged that pure quiescence-debounce converges on the prompt echo during model think-time — fixed at the root by converging on child-exit (is_eof) instead of hand-waving the echo away.
carry_forward_bullets: Multi-turn conversation (a prompt queue, converge after the last) + bidirectional AI<->AI relay (agent A's reply becomes agent B's prompt) — the full '<->'; this round makes one side real (one-shot).
Real token/$ cost accounting (claude -p --output-format json carries usage) to replace the injected-bytes guardrail proxy; needs a cost channel on Step/Driver, not just the byte count.

Interactive-TUI adapters (alt-screen, spinners, non-line-oriented capture) are harder than print-mode; the CLI's --ax-screen-reader flat mode may help. Echo-stripping (capture currently includes the prompt's cooked-mode echo) and scrollback capture (a reply that scrolls loses the off-screen rows) are also deferred.
Interactive cancel (still designed/deferred from R11): an Arc<AtomicBool> trigger + a cancelled statechart final + OutcomeState::Cancelled.

Round 13.decision_summary: Bidirectional AI<->AI: a Dialogue plugin runs two one-shot AI endpoints (claude -p) in alternating turns, spawning a fresh pane per turn via a new pane-lifecycle extension, capturing the threaded transcript.
changes_bullets: New crate file crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: the Dialogue plugin. Each step() is one turn — spawn the active endpoint as a fresh pane with the OTHER side's last message as its argv prompt (claude -p "<msg>"; message-as-argv, not stdin, so there is no cooked-mode echo to strip and the fresh pane's whole screen is the reply), await child-exit (R12 pane_eof), capture the reply, close the pane, hand the reply to the other side. Never self-converges; the Driver's max_iterations IS the turn budget (ends Exhausted with the transcript as payload — the Pipe pattern). Pinion-free.

Pane-lifecycle extension: new PaneLifecycle sub-trait {spawn(argv, cols, rows)->PaneId, close(id)->bool} reached via PaneAccess::lifecycle()->Option<&dyn PaneLifecycle> (default None) — kept OFF the read/inject surface every plugin depends on (interface segregation, zero ripple to Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent/test-doubles). WorkspacePaneAccess impls it over Workspace::spawn/close; new InjectError::Spawn. A RAII PaneGuard closes the per-turn pane on EVERY exit path (no leaked PTY/child even on a mid-step failure); close binds the removed Pane so its blocking Drop runs OUTSIDE the workspace lock (R11 lesson).
Honest accounting: Dialogue injects nothing (the message rides as argv), so Step.injected_bytes is 0 and the turn budget is purely max_iterations — no faking a byte cost into the guardrail.

Host wiring (sprag-host/plugins.rs): PluginsExternal 'dialogue' run arm (endpoint_a/endpoint_b argv arrays + seed + optional cols/rows/timeout_ms; NO target-pane validation — Dialogue creates its own panes), BoxedPlugin::Dialogue, PLUGINS += 'dialogue', a require_string_array argv helper. The transcript rides the R12 captured()/RunState.output seam. No new pinion RPC methods, no new SCXML states/events.
verification_bullets: 76 workspace tests pass (+8): access lifecycle_spawn_and_close_roundtrip + lifecycle_spawn_rejects_empty_argv; dialogue multi_turn_single_endpoint_threads_the_message, bidirectional_turns_alternate_endpoints (A:x -> B:A:x -> A:B:A:x -> B:A:B:A:x), leaves_no_leftover_panes, closes_the_pane_when_a_turn_times_out (the PaneGuard leak regression), no_lifecycle_fails_cleanly (NoPanes -> Failed); rpc runs_a_dialogue_plugin_to_done_with_a_transcript (background run, threaded transcript in output, only the initial pane survives). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

Genuine AI<->AI verified manually: the #[ignore]d dialogue::tests::two_real_claudes_converse ran two real 'claude -p' turns and captured a non-empty transcript (~10.8s). Offline coverage uses deterministic printf fake endpoints; the turn-threading logic is pinned by bidirectional_turns_alternate_endpoints so the live test only proves the real-CLI end to end.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: confirmed NO pinion/SCE change (a never-converge/exhaust-on-budget plugin is the existing Pipe shape on the existing statechart). It caught the pane-leak-on-early-return (-> the mandatory RAII PaneGuard), pushed back on fattening PaneAccess (-> the lifecycle() sub-trait accessor, ISP-clean), and on repurposing injected_bytes as reply bytes (-> honest 0).
carry_forward_bullets: Stateful conversation: turns are STATELESS (each side sees only the other's last message — a telephone game, not memory-preserving dialogue). Add context accumulation via claude -p --resume / session ids, or whole-history prompts.

Real token/$ cost accounting (claude -p --output-format json carries usage) to replace the injected-bytes guardrail proxy — now doubly relevant since Dialogue reports 0 injected bytes and only max_iterations bounds it.

Capture limits inherited from R12: a reply that scrolls past the pane loses the off-screen rows (no scrollback projection yet); a peer that paints a UI frame would pollute the captured text (print-mode tools like claude -p do not). Interactive-TUI adapters still deferred.

Interactive cancel (designed since R11): an Arc<AtomicBool> trigger + a cancelled statechart final + OutcomeState::Cancelled — increasingly wanted now that runs spawn real network-bound child processes.

Pane-lifecycle extension: new PaneLifecycle sub-trait {spawn(argv, cols, rows)->PaneId, close(id)->bool} reached via PaneAccess::lifecycle()->Option<&dyn PaneLifecycle> (default None) — kept OFF the read/inject surface every plugin depends on (interface segregation, zero ripple to Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent/test-doubles). WorkspacePaneAccess impls it over Workspace::spawn/close; new InjectError::Spawn. A RAII PaneGuard closes the per-turn pane on EVERY exit path (no leaked PTY/child even on a mid-step failure); close binds the removed Pane so its blocking Drop runs OUTSIDE the workspace lock (R11 lesson).
Honest accounting: Dialogue injects nothing (the message rides as argv), so Step.injected_bytes is 0 and the turn budget is purely max_iterations — no faking a byte cost into the guardrail.

Host wiring (sprag-host/plugins.rs): PluginsExternal 'dialogue' run arm (endpoint_a/endpoint_b argv arrays + seed + optional cols/rows/timeout_ms; NO target-pane validation — Dialogue creates its own panes), BoxedPlugin::Dialogue, PLUGINS += 'dialogue', a require_string_array argv helper. The transcript rides the R12 captured()/RunState.output seam. No new pinion RPC methods, no new SCXML states/events.

changes_bullets: orchestration.scxml: added a `cancel` transition out of `running` to a new `<final id="cancelled"/>` — SCE regenerated OrchestrationEvent::Cancel / OrchestrationState::Cancelled (another statechart final, the SCE dogfood). driver.rs: new OutcomeState::Cancelled; Driver::run checks panes.cancelled() at the loop TOP (fires Cancel before stepping, so a cancel pre-empts the next step); outcome() maps Cancelled explicitly, above the Failed wildcard.

Round 17.decision_summary: Textbook remediation of the AI layer: fix the smells the session review found — RunContext cancel seam, shared poll_until, coherent cost guardrail, lossless capture, single-source screen text, and SSOT/comment sync — without reworking the verified-clean foundation.
changes_bullets: Cancel seam (ISP fix): removed PaneAccess::cancelled (a run-lifecycle signal smuggled onto a pane-scoped trait); new RunContext in crates/sprag-plugin/src/run.rs threaded into Plugin::step and Driver::run, built host-side from the run's Arc<AtomicBool>. Each client now depends only on what it uses.

De-duplicated the await loops: the three hand-rolled bounded-cancellable waits (Orchestrator::observe, Agent::await_reply, Dialogue's await) collapse to one shared run::poll_until returning a Waited enum; shared POLL_INTERVAL + DEFAULT_REPLY_TIMEOUT constants (the per-plugin copies are gone).

Coherent cost guardrail: Step.injected_bytes -> Step.cost, Guardrails.max_injected_bytes -> max_cost; Dialogue now reports its argv prompt bytes (was a hardcoded 0), so the budget binds every plugin in one currency rather than being inert for the heaviest one.

Lossless capture: Dialogue stops flattening replies (removed split_whitespace().join) — replies are kept verbatim in a structured Vec<Turn>, rendered blank-line-delimited (render_turn) so code/lists/multi-line answers survive and turn boundaries stay clear.

Single-source screen text + corrections: Screen::full_text (sprag-vt) is the one definition, read by both in-process pane_full_text and a NEW RPC full_text query on the pane External (RPC peers and plugins now see the same screen, scrollback included). ED-3 (ESC[3J) now clears scrollback (was a no-op under a now-false comment). InjectError -> PaneError (covers spawn); BoxedPlugin -> PluginKind. Round 18.decision_summary: Replace the byte-proxy cost in the AI dialogue with real billed tokens parsed from `claude -p --output-format json`, reading the envelope from a new raw-stdout producer tap (the grid corrupts the wrapped single-line JSON) and degrading gracefully on any parse failure.
changes_bullets: sprag-terminal raw tap (crates/sprag-terminal/src/session.rs): TerminalSession gains a bounded, HEAD-anchored RawCapture (Arc<Mutex>, RAW_CAPTURE_CAP=256 KiB) the reader thread tees into in the SAME loop iteration as emulator.advance, so once is_eof holds every byte is BOTH captured and rendered (the grid's completeness guarantee extended to the source stream). SessionHandle::raw_output()/TerminalSession::raw_output() snapshot (bytes, truncated). Head-anchored (append-until-cap then latch truncated) because a JSON envelope is parsed from its START -- a tail ring would drop the opening brace; the cap is the oversized-degradation point. The lock() helper was generalized to any Mutex<T>.

PaneAccess::pane_raw_output (crates/sprag-plugin/src/access.rs): new pane_raw_output(id)->Option<(Vec<u8>,bool)>, DEFAULT None (interface segregation, like lifecycle() -- the three PaneAccess test doubles compile untouched); WorkspacePaneAccess returns the handle's raw snapshot. Documented as a distinct read (source bytes) from the pane_*_text family (rendered grid: wrapped, trailing-trimmed, control-stripped) -- NOT a read-path divergence (R17 unified the grid-text read), a legitimately different datum.

Reply parser (new crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs): parse_claude_json(&[u8])->Option<ClaudeReply{text:Option<String>,tokens:Option<u64>,is_error:bool}>, Value-walked (serde_json added to sprag-plugin as foreign-tool PERCEPTION, not type serialization -- the public surface stays serde-free, no derives). Brace-span ({..}) extraction tolerates a trailing newline / kernel ONLCR \r\n / framing noise. tokens = usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens (cache_creation/cache_read excluded -- large and bursty, would void a token budget). Requires a result/usage signature so a random JSON object is not claimed; any failure -> None.

ReplyFormat + Dialogue cost/capture (crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs): new ReplyFormat{Text(default), ClaudeJson} per-endpoint (DialogueSpec.format_a/format_b, mirroring label_a/label_b -- deferred the Endpoint-struct refactor). decode_reply: Text reads the rendered full_text (unchanged); ClaudeJson reads pane_raw_output, parses it, and on success records the result-text + real tokens. Graceful degradation: a truncated/over-cap/unparsable envelope falls back to the raw lossy text + the prompt-byte proxy cost -- never a PaneError, so a broken reply never fails the turn; the cancel path keeps the prompt-byte cost. Step.cost is now real tokens for a ClaudeJson turn.

Cost-unit contract (plugin.rs Step::cost / driver.rs Guardrails::max_cost docs): retired the 'one currency / bytes' framing for 'each plugin's natural spend unit; a run drives exactly ONE plugin so the caller sizes max_cost to it; the Driver stays unit-agnostic (only sums and bounds)'. NO Driver/SCXML/SCE change -- the cost channel R17 built IS the seam; only what feeds it changed.

Host (crates/sprag-host/src/plugins.rs): the dialogue run arm parses optional format_a/format_b ('text'|'claude_json'; unknown -> synchronous Rejected) via a new parse_reply_format helper; ReplyFormat re-exported from sprag-plugin.
verification_bullets: 106 workspace tests pass (+17 over R17's 89), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New deterministic tests: sprag-terminal raw_output byte-faithful-on-a-wrapping-line + over-cap-truncation; sprag-plugin reply parser (real envelope, escaped-\n preserved, framing noise, truncated/garbage/non-envelope -> None, is_error, missing-usage, usage-without-result), pane_raw_output round-trip, dialogue claude_json real-token-cost (cost==2 turns x 50) + token-bound guardrail (50-token budget exhausts in 1 turn) + graceful-degradation-on-bad-JSON (records raw text, does NOT Fail); sprag-host runs_a_claude_json_dialogue_with_real_token_cost (cost==100 over RPC, clean result not raw envelope) + rejects_an_unknown_reply_format.

Live AI re-verified: the #[ignore]d two_real_claudes_converse ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~22s) and accumulated real token cost = 18214 (a byte proxy would be a few hundred); the transcript carried the clean result text (no input_tokens envelope leak) and a coherent count -- the real-PTY check that the envelope parses off the raw source with no stderr/spinner/wrap pollution.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent (read every touched file first): confirmed the raw-stdout tap is the correct seam over the lossy grid (pane_full_text injects a wrap-\n at every row; trailing-trim drops interior spaces in result), the cost unit is total tokens (exact integer, keeps the 64*1024 default guardrail sane) not micro-USD, ReplyFormat is per-endpoint fields not an Endpoint-struct refactor (deferred), serde_json-for-perception does not breach the serde-free contract, and the eof-ordering tee is the correctness linchpin. NO pinion / SCE / SCXML / sprag-vt change.
carry_forward_bullets: --resume for Dialogue: reuse the session_id the JSON envelope already carries (parsed but unused this round) to avoid the O(n^2) whole-history argv resend + the MAX_ARG_STRLEN single-arg ceiling -- the natural next round, directly synergizing with this one.

Agent token cost: Agent still reports injected bytes and reads the visible damage-delta. The raw tap is clean only for Dialogue's FRESH-pane argv model -- Agent injects into a non-fresh pane, so its raw stdout interleaves the cooked-mode prompt echo with the reply. A shared one-shot-exchange abstraction could let Agent adopt parse_claude_json once a clean reply-region read exists.

total_cost_usd ($) is parsed off the envelope but not surfaced: Outcome carries one integer cost (tokens). A $ display channel belongs on the captured-content (display) side, not the guardrail, if wanted later.

The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse the endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b field sprawl into one cohesive per-side struct) is the recommended dedicated follow-up now that ReplyFormat proved the per-endpoint concept.
Raw capture is bounded at 256 KiB head-anchored: a >256 KiB single reply truncates -> parse fails -> graceful byte-proxy fallback (a documented bound, not silent corruption).

Round 19.decision_summary: Neutralize the decoded-reply type name to mark the abstraction boundary surfaced by review: the decoded shape is tool-agnostic (AgentReply), while the parser and format variant stay tool-specific (parse_claude_json / ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson) because AI-tool JSON schemas are not standardized.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs + lib.rs: renamed ClaudeReply -> AgentReply (the tool-agnostic decoded shape: text + tokens + is_error); parse_claude_json now returns AgentReply, and the struct/module doc generalized to 'a decoded agent reply, independent of which tool produced it'. The parser parse_claude_json and the per-endpoint ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson stay claude-named ON PURPOSE -- they encode claude's specific envelope schema (result / usage.input_tokens), and a generic 'Json' name would be a false abstraction since no cross-tool AI-JSON standard exists.

Made the extension path for a second print-mode-JSON agent explicit: add a ReplyFormat variant + a parser mapping that tool's envelope onto the SAME AgentReply + one decode_reply match arm + one host arg mapping (~30 lines). The raw-stdout tap (pane_raw_output), the cost channel (Step::cost), and the graceful-degradation fallback are already tool-agnostic, so no new result type and no foundation change. An interactive-TUI agent (non print-mode) remains the harder, separately-tracked capture problem.
verification_bullets: Pure rename, no behavior change: 106 workspace tests pass, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; grep confirms zero ClaudeReply references remain. Prompted by a design question (could the R18 cost path serve a non-claude agent?) -- the answer is yes via the enum+parser seam, and the result type is now named so the shape reads as generic while the parser reads as specific.
carry_forward_bullets: When a second AgentReply producer lands, split the parsers into per-tool modules (e.g. reply::claude / reply::<tool>) under the shared AgentReply + a ReplyFormat variant each; only then is a trait-object decoder (vs the enum) worth its registry machinery (YAGNI until an out-of-tree decoder appears).

Round 20.decision_summary: Make a ClaudeJson Dialogue resume each side's server session (claude -p --resume <session_id>) and send only the peer's last message, replacing the O(n^2) whole-history resend; a resume that returns no session id self-heals to the fresh whole-history path.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs: AgentReply gains session_id: Option<String>, extracted from the envelope's session_id key (previously unread). A real-CLI probe confirmed the id is STABLE across a resume, so a side keeps ONE id for the whole run.

crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: Dialogue holds sessions: [Option<String>; 2] indexed by turn%2 and selected by the SAME parity branch as endpoint/label/format (one SSOT, no drifting second branch). A side's FIRST turn (session None) and every Text endpoint take the UNCHANGED whole-history render_prompt; a ClaudeJson side that already holds a session RESUMES: argv gets ['--resume', id] before the prompt, and the prompt is a new render_resume_prompt = just the peer's last turn (render_turn(history.last())) since the server holds this side's prior context. History still accumulates for the transcript and the fresh/Text path.

decode_reply / decode_claude_json now return a named DecodedTurn{text, cost, session_id} (was a (String,u64) tuple). step() stores the id on every reply that carries one (idempotent; an is_error reply WITH an id is still a continuable session), and RESETS the side to None only when a RESUME turn returns NO id (bad/expired id, or a garbled envelope) -- self-healing to the whole-history fresh path on the next same-side turn. A broken resume never fails the turn (the R18 graceful-degradation philosophy).

Resume is automatic and internal -- gated by ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson + session presence, so NO new spec field, NO RPC arg, NO sprag-host change. NO statechart change (the Step{cost,verdict} contract is unchanged; verdict stays Continue every turn). Only sprag-plugin (reply.rs + dialogue.rs) changed; lib.rs re-exports unchanged (the new AgentReply field rides the existing export).
verification_bullets: 109 workspace tests pass (+3 over R19's 106), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New network-free tests: reply extracts_session_id_when_present + missing_session_id_yields_none; dialogue claude_json_resumes_after_the_first_turn (an argv-self-inspecting fake proves --resume appears on turn 2+ of EACH side but not turn 1) + resume_failure_self_heals_to_fresh (a fake emitting non-JSON on a --resume call -> the side resets and its next turn parses cleanly again). All prior tests unchanged -- the Text and json_fake paths emit no session_id so they stay on the fresh path.

Live AI re-verified: two_real_claudes_converse (now exercising --resume on turns 2-3) ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) with a coherent count ACROSS the resumed turns (proves the server preserved context via --resume). Real token cost = 9129, roughly HALF of R18's 18214 for the same 4-turn conversation -- direct evidence resume cut the per-turn input tokens (delta-only prompts vs whole-history resend).

Probe-grounded (real 2-turn CLI run): claude -p --output-format json --resume <id> works with the prompt as the final positional arg; the session_id is stable across resume; context is preserved (a resumed turn recalled a fact from turn 1). Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: it endorsed the single-parity-index session shape, the DecodedTurn struct over a tuple, and SHARPENED the resume-failure trigger to 'reset only when a resume turn returns no session_id', NOT on is_error:true-with-id (a tool-side error on a live session is still continuable). NO pinion/SCE/SCXML/host change.
carry_forward_bullets: The real claude behavior for a bad/expired --resume id is UNVERIFIED at the CLI -- the deterministic self-heal test covers the MECHANISM (no-session-id-on-a-resume-turn -> reset), and the detector is robust to both a valid {is_error, no-session} envelope and a non-JSON error. Pin it only if a live bad-id case surfaces.

render_resume_prompt sends the peer's last turn labelled; the turn-0/1 fresh prompt established the per-side instruction in each server session, so the minimal resume prompt relies on that persisting (probe-confirmed). If a future model drifts without re-instruction, re-add a tiny per-turn framing to the resume prompt.
Agent (one-shot) does not use resume; a future multi-turn Agent could reuse this per-side session pattern. Agent token cost + clean reply-region capture remains the separate backlog item.
The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into one per-side struct) is still the recommended cohesion follow-up.

publishable_changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs: AgentReply gains session_id: Option<String>, extracted from the envelope's session_id key (previously unread). A real-CLI probe confirmed the id is STABLE across a resume, so a side keeps ONE id for the whole run.

crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: Dialogue holds sessions: [Option<String>; 2] indexed by turn%2 and selected by the SAME parity branch as endpoint/label/format (one SSOT, no drifting second branch). A side's FIRST turn (session None) and every Text endpoint take the UNCHANGED whole-history render_prompt; a ClaudeJson side that already holds a session RESUMES: argv gets ['--resume', id] before the prompt, and the prompt is a new render_resume_prompt = just the peer's last turn (render_turn(history.last())) since the server holds this side's prior context. History still accumulates for the transcript and the fresh/Text path.

decode_reply / decode_claude_json now return a named DecodedTurn{text, cost, session_id} (was a (String,u64) tuple). step() stores the id on every reply that carries one (idempotent; an is_error reply WITH an id is still a continuable session), and RESETS the side to None only when a RESUME turn returns NO id (bad/expired id, or a garbled envelope) -- self-healing to the whole-history fresh path on the next same-side turn. A broken resume never fails the turn (the R18 graceful-degradation philosophy).

Resume is automatic and internal -- gated by ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson + session presence, so NO new spec field, NO RPC arg, NO sprag-host change. NO statechart change (the Step{cost,verdict} contract is unchanged; verdict stays Continue every turn). Only sprag-plugin (reply.rs + dialogue.rs) changed; lib.rs re-exports unchanged (the new AgentReply field rides the existing export).
publishable_verification_bullets: 109 workspace tests pass (+3 over R19's 106), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New network-free tests: reply extracts_session_id_when_present + missing_session_id_yields_none; dialogue claude_json_resumes_after_the_first_turn (an argv-self-inspecting fake proves --resume appears on turn 2+ of EACH side but not turn 1) + resume_failure_self_heals_to_fresh (a fake emitting non-JSON on a --resume call -> the side resets and its next turn parses cleanly again). All prior tests unchanged -- the Text and json_fake paths emit no session_id so they stay on the fresh path.

Live AI re-verified: two_real_claudes_converse (now exercising --resume on turns 2-3) ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) with a coherent count ACROSS the resumed turns (proves the server preserved context via --resume). Real token cost = 9129, roughly HALF of R18's 18214 for the same 4-turn conversation -- direct evidence resume cut the per-turn input tokens (delta-only prompts vs whole-history resend).

Probe-grounded (real 2-turn CLI run): claude -p --output-format json --resume <id> works with the prompt as the final positional arg; the session_id is stable across resume; context is preserved (a resumed turn recalled a fact from turn 1). Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: it endorsed the single-parity-index session shape, the DecodedTurn struct over a tuple, and SHARPENED the resume-failure trigger to 'reset only when a resume turn returns no session_id', NOT on is_error:true-with-id (a tool-side error on a live session is still continuable). NO pinion/SCE/SCXML/host change.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: The real claude behavior for a bad/expired --resume id is UNVERIFIED at the CLI -- the deterministic self-heal test covers the MECHANISM (no-session-id-on-a-resume-turn -> reset), and the detector is robust to both a valid {is_error, no-session} envelope and a non-JSON error. Pin it only if a live bad-id case surfaces.

render_resume_prompt sends the peer's last turn labelled; the turn-0/1 fresh prompt established the per-side instruction in each server session, so the minimal resume prompt relies on that persisting (probe-confirmed). If a future model drifts without re-instruction, re-add a tiny per-turn framing to the resume prompt.
Agent (one-shot) does not use resume; a future multi-turn Agent could reuse this per-side session pattern. Agent token cost + clean reply-region capture remains the separate backlog item.
The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into one per-side struct) is still the recommended cohesion follow-up.

Round 21.decision_summary: R21 remediation of the AI layer: a typed Cost (Bytes vs Tokens, one unit per plugin) replaces the unit-mixing u64 cost and retires the byte proxy; raw-byte capture moves off PaneAccess into a PaneRawCapture sub-trait; and the empty-result envelope leak, the unused AgentReply.is_error field, and stale cost/SSOT docs are fixed.
changes_bullets: Typed cost (plugin.rs/driver.rs): new enum Cost{Bytes(u64),Tokens(u64)} on Step::cost; the Driver accumulates Option<Cost> (one unit per run, a mid-run unit change is debug-asserted via Cost::try_add), Guardrails::max_cost and Outcome::cost become Option<Cost>, and budget_exhausted compares like-with-like via Cost::reaches. The byte-relay plugins (Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent) report Cost::Bytes; Dialogue is uniformly TOKEN-denominated, so the byte proxy (prompt_cost/fallback_cost) is fully RETIRED -- a Text endpoint, a degraded ClaudeJson reply, and a cancelled turn all report Tokens(0) (no measured spend), with max_iterations as the liveness floor.

Host (sprag-host/plugins.rs): DEFAULT_GUARDRAILS split into DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS / DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES / DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS(200k); PluginKind::default_cost() carries each plugin's unit; build_plugin now runs BEFORE parse_guardrails, which reads a bare wire max_cost in that unit (cost_in_unit_of); outcome_to_json emits a self-describing {cost, unit} so a peer reads the cost without knowing the plugin.

RawOutput struct (sprag-terminal/session.rs): the raw-capture (Vec<u8>,bool) tuple is now a named RawOutput{bytes,truncated}, re-exported and destructured at every seam (session.rs, access.rs, dialogue.rs) -- named like PaneRow.

PaneRawCapture sub-trait (sprag-plugin/access.rs): pane_raw_output moved OFF PaneAccess (the scene-as-data extension surface) into a PaneRawCapture trait reached via raw_capture()->Option<&dyn PaneRawCapture>, mirroring PaneLifecycle/lifecycle(). The core invariant 'a plugin reads structured screen data, never raw bytes' is now STRUCTURAL -- only a plugin that asks for the capability can reach raw bytes; Dialogue reaches it via panes.raw_capture().

Empty-result leak (dialogue.rs decode_claude_json): a cleanly-parsed envelope with an empty/missing result now records an EMPTY turn (reply.text.unwrap_or_default()), not the whole JSON envelope; the raw-text fallback is confined to the parse-FAILED arm, so a result-less reply no longer leaks usage/session_id into the transcript or the next prompt. Real tokens are still billed.

YAGNI + doc/SSOT: dropped the unused AgentReply.is_error field + its parse (no consumer read it -- self-heal keys on session_id); the error-envelope test now asserts text/tokens still extract through the ignored key. Restored the cache-token-exclusion rationale (large/bursty would void a token budget) on tokens/parse_tokens; corrected Step::cost's 'positive/monotonic' doc to 'non-negative, Tokens(0) possible, iterations is the liveness guarantee'; fixed render_turn's doc (the blank-line join is at the call sites, not in render_turn); threaded Guardrails through the dialogue test run_with() helper so the cost-binding test stops inlining a Driver.
verification_bullets: 110 workspace tests pass (+1: clean_empty_result_records_an_empty_turn_not_the_envelope), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. Cost tests migrated to the typed value: claude_json_degrades_on_unparsable_reply flips from cost>0 (the old byte proxy) to Some(Cost::Tokens(0)); claude_json_reply_reports_real_token_cost asserts Some(Cost::Tokens(100)); the orchestrator byte-budget test asserts Some(Cost::Bytes(n)); the RPC dialogue test asserts cost==100 AND unit=='tokens'.

Live-verified (touches the AI path): two_real_claudes_converse, now under typed Cost, ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) and accumulated real token cost Some(Tokens(9095)) -- coherent with R20's ~9129 -- with a clean transcript and no envelope leak. The typed-tokens path works end-to-end with real claude.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent, then SHARPENED in an adversarial review: the agent recommended a two-balance (parallel bytes+tokens) budget to accommodate a heterogeneous Dialogue, but a from-first-principles pass identified the byte proxy as the root smell -- retiring it makes 'one plugin = one unit' structurally TRUE, so a single typed Cost (not two parallel balances) is the more textbook, SSOT-respecting seam, closer to this round's original 'Driver refuses to sum across units' intent. Confirmed NO SCXML / SCE-codegen change (orchestration.scxml is datamodel=null; the cost accumulator is plain Rust around the engine).
carry_forward_bullets: Deferred WITH rationale: per-pane OPT-IN raw capture (today every TerminalSession carries a 256 KiB-capable RawCapture buffer even for a shell/cat pane that never reads it) -- it crosses into the producer crate's spawn signature, so it stays an R22 candidate; PaneRawCapture now makes it implementable with no further API churn (raw_capture() can return None for an opt-out pane).

Conversation/session collaborator extraction from the Dialogue god-plugin (the fresh->resumed->reset session lifecycle is a hand-rolled state machine that belongs in SCE -- the dogfood) plus the Endpoint{argv,format,label} struct (collapsing endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b): still deferred.

Interactive-TUI agent seam + a ReplyDecoder trait the PLUGIN supplies (vs the closed in-crate ReplyFormat enum), due when a 2nd AI-tool adapter lands -- the architecture lens called that the north star's defining event. Typed Cost already clarifies its contract: a decoder returns Cost, not u64.

Agent still reports Cost::Bytes (injected) and reads the visible damage-delta (it injects into a non-fresh pane); a clean reply-region read + parse_claude_json adoption is the natural 'third consumer' that would justify a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction.

total_cost_usd ($) display channel belongs on the captured-content side, not the guardrail. pinion R1.6 GPU glyph paint LANDED (R991/384f2f4) so the GUI windowed-host is newly unblocked for GPU text, but pending the cursor slice + the whole TUI backend; sprag still builds NO bespoke renderer.
