Round 21.1.decision_summary: Post-R21 adversarial session review (refactoring + architecture lenses + direct SSOT cross-check) found R21 mechanically sound and the single-typed-Cost decision correct, but NOT fully textbook; the R21.1 clearance fixes the shared must-fix + the majors.
changes_bullets: Dead-API + open/closed (plugin.rs/plugins.rs): both reviewers independently flagged `Cost::amount()` as dead public API while the host re-matched variants inline. Added `Cost::unit() -> &'static str` (the single variant->label mapping), and `outcome_to_json` now does `outcome.cost.map_or((0,None), |c| (c.amount(), Some(c.unit())))` — so the host NEVER names a `Cost` variant. A new cost unit now edits only plugin.rs + `PluginKind::default_cost` (the legitimate plugin->unit map), not the host's render/parse.

Silent fail-open (plugin.rs): `Cost::reaches`'s unit-mismatch arm returned `false` with no guard — a disarmed spend guardrail failing silently. Added a `debug_assert!(false, ...)` (matching `accumulate`'s `try_add` guard) so a mismatch screams in debug and still reports not-reached (iteration-bounded) in release.

Self-describing guardrail wire (plugins.rs/rpc.rs): replaced the unit-BLIND bare `max_cost` (a dialogue caller could load a byte-intended number as a 64x-looser TOKEN bound with no feedback) with self-describing `max_bytes` XOR `max_tokens`, validated against the plugin's unit via `Cost::unit()` — wrong unit / both keys -> synchronous `Rejected` (new `parse_max_cost`, removed `cost_in_unit_of`). New test `rejects_a_wrong_unit_guardrail`; 6 RPC wire sites migrated.

Honest docs (plugins.rs): the module header + `parse_guardrails` no longer claim a cost bound that a `Tokens(0)`-only (print-mode Text) dialogue cannot deliver — they now state iterations are its sole effective bound, by design. `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` is documented as a COARSE backstop (cache tokens excluded; the iteration cap is primary), not a precise spend bound.

Stale-doc sweep (dialogue.rs/reply.rs): rewrote the PUBLIC `ReplyFormat::Text`/`ClaudeJson` docs (still said 'prompt-byte proxy' / 'degrades to the byte proxy' — false after R21 retired it; now `Tokens(0)`), fixed a degrades-test comment that CONTRADICTED its own `Tokens(0)` assertion, and swept the remaining byte-proxy mentions in reply.rs module/parse docs and the test contrast comments.
verification_bullets: 111 workspace tests pass (+1: rejects_a_wrong_unit_guardrail; sprag-host 33, sprag-plugin 37 +2 ignored), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. R21.1 touches only docs, a new Cost::unit(), the release-inert reaches debug-guard, and the host wire (fully covered by the deterministic RPC tests) -- it does NOT touch the token decode/accumulate path R21 already live-verified, so the live AI test was consciously not re-run (unchanged, covered).

Driven by two independent adversarial reviewers (a refactoring lens + an architecture lens) over `git diff f1688a3 9b03d2a` plus a direct SSOT grep. They CONVERGED on the dead `amount()` + the stale byte-proxy docs (both must-fix). The architecture lens explicitly RULED the R21 single-typed-Cost decision correct over the Plan agent's two-balance (two-balance bakes 'exactly two units forever' into the Driver/Guardrails shape -- the real open/closed violation). The clearance addressed every must-fix and major they raised.
carry_forward_bullets: is_error (architecture lens, deferred WITH rationale): the review flagged that R21 dropped `AgentReply.is_error` -- the one structured ERROR bit in the tool-agnostic decoded shape -- as an implicit capability narrowing (a future 'stop the dialogue when a side errors' policy would want it). Decision: KEEP it removed (the project's own YAGNI / no-dead-surface rule; re-adding a consumer-less bool re-introduces the exact smell R21 removed), and re-add `is_error` + its parse line TOGETHER with the error-aware-orchestration policy that consumes it. The error-envelope parse-tolerance test already proves the flag's key does not derail parsing when it returns.

Cost open/closed is now clean: a hypothetical `Cost::Dollars` edits only plugin.rs (the enum + amount/unit/try_add/reaches arms, all next to the type) and `PluginKind::default_cost` (the plugin->unit assignment) -- the host's outcome rendering and guardrail parsing are variant-name-free via `unit()`/`amount()`.

The Outcome::cost `Option<Cost>` double-optionality (None only on a cancel-at-loop-top, 0-step run) was reviewed and kept: seeding a concrete zero needs a unit the Driver lacks when max_cost is None, so Option is the honest model.

Round 22.decision_summary: Decompose the Dialogue god-plugin into an Endpoint struct (collapsing the parallel endpoint/label/format field pairs) and a Session collaborator whose fresh/resumed/reset server-session lifecycle is sprag's second SCE statechart (the dogfood), unblocked by an upstream SCE +Send fix on Engine's boxed callbacks.
changes_bullets: Endpoint struct (sprag-plugin/dialogue.rs): collapsed the six parallel fields endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into Endpoint{argv,label,format} and DialogueSpec.endpoints: [Endpoint; 2]; the turn%2 parity now selects ONE Endpoint so argv/label/format cannot drift apart. DialogueSpec::new(argv_a,argv_b,seed) keeps its signature (defaults labels A/B + ReplyFormat::Text); Endpoint re-exported (a public field type).

Session collaborator (new sprag-plugin/session.rs + session.scxml): a per-endpoint server-session lifecycle modeled as a 2-state REACTIVE SCE statechart (states fresh/resumed, events opened/absent, NO <final>, datamodel=null) — sprag's SECOND SCE machine after the Driver's orchestration.scxml (the dogfood generalizing the build to N machines). Session{engine: Engine<SessionPolicy>, id} holds the id String beside the engine (a null datamodel cannot hold it, like the Driver's counters beside its lifecycle machine). resuming()->Option<&str> is Some iff resumed; record(Option<String>) folds a decoded id into the lifecycle, ordered store-then-Opened / Absent-then-clear.

Dialogue integration: replaced sessions:[Option<String>;2] + the hand-rolled match decoded.session_id { Some=>store, None if resume=>reset, None=>{} } with sessions:[Session;2] + Session::record. The resume gate format==ClaudeJson && session.is_some() collapsed to resuming().is_some() (state==resumed) — SUBSUMED because a Text turn decodes to no id so its Session stays fresh forever. The reset rule (a resume returning no id => fresh) is now the resumed--absent-->fresh transition. step() clones argv/label/format and the resume id out before the spawn (borrow discipline).

The state<->id invariant: after every record, (state==resumed) <=> id.is_some(), debug_asserted — LOAD-BEARING, a Plan-agent + adversarial design pass identified it as what makes the new state-based resume/reset gate equivalent to the old intent-based resume bool (documented in session.rs).

build/codegen (build.rs, lib.rs, driver.rs): build.rs compiles BOTH statecharts via a STATECHARTS stem list and generalizes the inner-attr strip to each generated file; the sm module split into sm::orchestration + sm::session submodules (each its own include! so the duplicate generated use lines stay isolated); driver.rs import path updated; PluginKind::Dialogue boxed (the two embedded session engines made it a clippy large_enum_variant).

changes_bullets: sprag-gui: access_node returns one terminal_a11y_node (pure helper) over the boot pane - AriaRole::Group (not TextInput: pinion has no terminal/log role, and a textbox would advertise caret/set-value edit affordances the PTY-keystroke widget does not implement), name = "Terminal: <command>", value = AccessValue::Text(screen full_text), focused = (focus == ROOT_TAG).
The screen text reuses Screen::full_text - the same SSOT string the RPC full_text query and the plugin capture read, so the AT and the AI see one notion of the screen (scrollback + visible).
The node tag is ROOT_TAG, shared with the keyboard focus gate (apply_key) and the paint-root container, so AT focus + bounds + the key focus gate share one identity.

Round 29.decision_summary: Round 29: add scrollback viewing to the GUI terminal - Shift+PageUp/PageDown scroll a history window over the pane's retained scrollback, reusing the one projection seam at a scrolled entry; the live view is unchanged.
changes_bullets: sprag-grid: project_scrolled(screen, offset_lines) windows offset_lines of scrollback above the live bottom, reusing project() (offset 0) + project_row() (visible rows) + history_row() (scrollback text -> default-color cells); a stale offset clamped to live returns project() WITH the cursor. History is text-only (the R16 scrollback model).

sprag-host: pane_view_scene_scrolled(.., offset) GUI seam; pane_view_scene delegates (offset 0, byte-identical); both assemble via a shared grid_node node-base + view_text_grid (the headless data path is unchanged).

sprag-gui: use_scroll_offset Signal (Owner::cache) + pure next_scroll_offset clamp + scroll_view; apply_key consumes Shift+PageUp/PageDown as a scroll (not to the PTY) and snaps to the live bottom on any typed key; view reads the offset. offset=0 follows with no drift.
verification_bullets: sprag-grid 6 + sprag-host 34 + sprag-gui 11 tests pass (project_scrolled windowing + stale-offset cursor clamp; pure next_scroll_offset clamp/saturate; apply_key scroll-gate + snap-to-bottom); full sprag workspace 130, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean, cargo doc no new broken links.
Headless screenshot boots + renders 960x600 byte-identical to R26-R28 (offset 0 == project, paint-transparent).

Two adversarial reviewers cleared the windowing math / reactivity / layering / SSOT-reuse and caught a cursor-omit on a stale-offset-clamped-to-live path (fixed: early-return on the clamped offset) + an orphaned view doc + a node-base micro-duplication (both fixed).
carry_forward_bullets: Scrollback is text-only (R16 model) - history renders in default colors; a full-cell scrollback model (colors/attrs retained in history) is a sprag-vt enhancement, deferred.

Scroll-during-output drift: the offset is relative to the live bottom, so output arriving while scrolled shifts the view; an absolute (content-anchored) pin needs producer-side scrollback-growth reactivity, deferred.
Mouse / pointer->cell (R1.8) + multi-pane remain the next big directions (mouse = a pinion seam; multi-pane = an External-model restructure).

Round 30.decision_summary: Round 30: session-review remediation of R26-R29 (four-reviewer + grep audit) - extract a boot_pane() SSOT accessor unifying single-pane selection (5 sites / 3 absence idioms -> 1) and correct overstated/stale docs; no behavior change. The data-flow SSOT, concurrency, and pinion-boundary consumption were cleared as textbook.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui: TerminalView::boot_pane() -> &Pane is the one site answering "which pane?" - view / access_node / scroll_view / the reflow Effect / pane_handle all route through it (was 5 panes().first() sites with 3 different absence idioms: .expect / else-return / filter-map), unified to the documented boot-pane invariant so the multi-pane round generalizes pane selection in one place.

sprag-terminal: resize/dimensions docs corrected - they overstated atomicity (the PTY winsize ioctl precedes the emulator update by one uncontended lock, so a SIGWINCH-racing child may transiently observe the new winsize first; transient, visual-only, self-healing).

Doc/staleness: window title no longer round-pinned (omitted R28/R29); the "read-only behavior" comment reworded (frozen final screen, not a loss of interactivity); the a11y Group-over-Generic choice documented (a Generic container drops the accessible name).
verification_bullets: Four independent adversarial reviewers (architecture / SSOT / concurrency / pinion-boundary) + a repo-wide grep audit. Cleared as textbook: projection / winsize / screen-text / key-encoding / dimensions SSOT; no race / deadlock / leak / UAF (reader thread + Mutex + Drop graph traced); idiomatic seam consumption (the apply_key hand-roll is justified - forward_key_to_external cannot carry modifiers and has the wrong verdict mapping); the GUI is a faithful secondary path, never a second authority.

sprag-grid 6 + sprag-host 34 + sprag-gui 11 + sprag-terminal 8 = 59 tests pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; cargo doc no new broken links; headless screenshot byte-identical (121434) - the refactor is behavior-preserving.

Deferred (named, not hidden): scroll-during-output drift (proper fix = content-anchor needs producer-side scrollback-growth reactivity; the bounded FIFO has no stable line identity a pure view can track); main.rs modularization (762 lines, best paid at the multi-pane round); full-cell scrollback (R16 text-only model).
carry_forward_bullets: Multi-pane round: generalize boot_pane() -> active_pane() + per-pane tags (the ROOT_TAG singleton has 26 refs) + focused-pane input routing; modularize main.rs (terminal / reflow / input / a11y / view) at the same time.
Scroll content-anchoring: expose scrollback growth reactively from the producer (sprag-vt) so the GUI can pin the view to absolute content under output, removing the v1 bottom-relative drift.
Mouse / pointer->cell (R1.8) needs a pinion seam (a click delivered to a TextGrid widget with cell coords) - a separate spec-round, on the pinion side of the boundary.

Round 31.decision_summary: Round 31: IME-composed input (Hangul / CJK) routed to the PTY via a new literal-text seam. A composed commit is finished text, not a keystroke, so it must bypass the W3C key encoder: a sibling invoke("text", ...) action on SpragPaneExternal writes the committed UTF-8 directly to the child, and TerminalViewer::apply_composition (a WidgetCore override, focus-gated on ROOT_TAG, a faithful mirror of apply_key) drives it. Preedit stays off-grid, rendered by the platform IME; an inline on-grid preedit overlay is a later round.
changes_bullets: sprag-host: SpragPaneExternal gains a "text" invoke action (inject_text) writing literal UTF-8 to the PTY with no key-encoding - the seam for IME commits and paste, the same scene/invoke wire the AI peer drives (§2 #2). parse_text_args accepts a bare string or a {text:...} object (symmetric with the key parser); empty text is a no-op success (the IME cancel-via-empty-commit shape). The introspect schema lists text beside key.

sprag-gui: TerminalViewer::apply_composition (WidgetCore override) routes CompositionEvent::Commit to invoke("text", ...), focus-gated on ROOT_TAG and snapping the scrollback view to the live bottom - a faithful mirror of apply_key. Start/Update (preedit) and Cancel are not consumed; the platform IME renders the in-progress composition itself.

A composition commit is text, not a keystroke, so it deliberately bypasses sprag-input::encode (W3C key -> control bytes); the literal-text path is the textbook seam rather than fabricating synthetic keystrokes.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: all pass, 0 failed; 4 new tests - apply_composition_routes_committed_ime_text_to_the_pane (e2e: committed Hangul echoes back through a live cat PTY in cooked mode), parses_bare_string_text, parses_object_text, non_string_text_is_type_mismatch; the focus-gate, preedit (Update), and empty-commit cases asserted as deterministic no-ops.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean (exit 0); validate-workspace T1 orphan=0; entries 31 -> 32.

Audit-first against pinion: WidgetCore::apply_composition(scene, focused, event)->bool (default false) override confirmed; ShellCore::apply_composition sources focused via focus.focused() and runs V::apply_composition inside root_owner.run (so use_scroll_offset resolves an Owner); winit WindowEvent::Ime -> winit_ime_to_composition -> Commit is wired in pinion-shell app.rs; IntrospectValue::Text(String) is the literal payload variant.
carry_forward_bullets: Multi-pane: generalize boot_pane() -> active_pane() + per-pane tags (the ROOT_TAG singleton) + focused-pane input routing (key + composition + future mouse); modularize the 762-line main.rs (terminal / reflow / input / a11y / view) at the same time.

Scroll content-anchoring: expose scrollback growth reactively from the producer (sprag-vt) so the GUI pins the view to absolute content under output, removing the v1 bottom-relative drift. Full-cell scrollback (the R16 text-only history model loses colors) folds in here.

IME inline preedit overlay: the platform IME renders the in-progress composition off-grid; an on-grid preedit overlay (plus set_ime_cursor_area positioning) is a later round. Mouse / pointer->cell is now unblocked pinion-side (R1008 px_to_cell + R1009 named-key + R1010 focus-ring opt-out); the remaining sprag work is the pane mouse-report consumer (byte encoding + per-pane routing).

Round 34.decision_summary: Round 34: Korean/CJK IME made usable via an inline preedit overlay. Root cause found with live data (ibus-hangul over X11+XIM, driven by XTEST, read back as scene/snapshot DATA): the commit->PTY seam and multi-jamo coalescence already worked, but the in-progress preedit was invisible — under winit+XIM the platform IME emits Ime::Preedit for the app to render (it does not paint over-the-spot), and sprag ignored Update, so nothing showed until commit (the 'jamo dont coalesce live' symptom). Fix is fully sprag-side, no pinion change: route_composition mirrors Start/Update/Commit/Cancel into an Owner::cache preedit Signal, view overlays it underlined at the cursor via new seams (sprag_grid::overlay_preedit + sprag_host::pane_view_scene_scrolled_with_preedit), and returns true so the shells R705.1 reactive dirty bridge repaints live. Display-only: the preedit never reaches the PTY. ime_caret_rect (Hanja candidate positioning) remains unwired polish.

Verified: workspace tests + clippy clean; live ibus-hangul 한글 renders full-width (no regression).

Round 36.decision_summary: Round 36: multi-pane GUI — sprag-gui tiles N terminal panes (default 2, SPRAG_GUI_PANES), routes keystroke/IME input to the focused pane, cycles focus with Ctrl+PageUp/Down, and reflows each pane independently via pinion R1012 use_pane_viewport_size. No upstream gap (pinion already shipped the per-pane viewport seam for exactly this) and no window-side split math (the sub-rect is pinion's post-layout measure). D1 resolved with a PaneViewSpec struct; D2 with per-pane Owner::cache state; the host owns the tiling layout (the R25 lesson).

Round 37.decision_summary: Round 37: dock/undock — Ctrl+Shift+Enter detaches the focused terminal pane into its own OS window (and docks it back) via pinion's multi-window seam (windows_signal + view_for_window, the hello-dock-panels pattern). Input is unchanged (global model scene + global focus, so a key reaches the focused pane regardless of which window paints it); dock/undock changes only WHERE a pane is painted, so it does NOT hit the PR-9 dynamic-focusable gap. The undock window opens fixed to the pane's intrinsic (cols,rows) x cell — an honest v1 bound, since pinion's R1006/R1012 viewport publishes are gated to the default window (reported as PR-10 for resizable undock windows). Live-verified via XTEST: Ctrl+Shift+Enter opened a 2nd OS window.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui/dock (new module): the floating SSOT is the window topology Signal<Vec<WindowSpec>> itself (a pane floats iff its pane-{i} window exists). use_windows_topology (root-owner cached), pane_window_id/pane_window_index (total fn, validated < MAX_PANES), is_pane_floating, toggle_pane_floating (push/remove a WindowSpec sized to the pane's own (cols,rows) x cell — NOT a window-side split calc).

sprag-gui/main: WidgetView::windows_signal returns the dock topology (opt into runtime windows); view_for_window dispatches per window (main tiles the docked panes, pane-{i} paints that pane); WidgetCore::view delegates to the main path (windowless/RPC fallback).

sprag-gui/view: one per-pane builder (build_pane_scene) shared by view_main (tile DOCKED panes only) and an undock window (one pane); view_for_window dispatch; an all-floated main is a childless Container (no panic).

sprag-gui/input: route_key Ctrl+Shift+Enter toggles the focused pane's dock state (toggle_pane_floating + focus_request), returns true, reaches no PTY — sibling of the Ctrl+PageUp/Down focus-cycle and Shift+PageUp/Down scroll chords; Ctrl+Shift+Enter is essentially unbound in TUIs.
sprag-gui/a11y: per-window access_nodes_for_window (main = docked panes, pane-{i} = that one pane) so a sibling window's AT tree carries no ghost nodes; shared pane_node builder.

No host / sprag-terminal change, no pinion edit: the model scene, input routing, focusable_tags, and the per-pane reflow Effects are all unchanged (a floated pane's reflow Effect stays inert — it reads (0,0) from the main publish where it is absent — keeping its last docked size).
verification_bullets: 155 workspace tests pass (sprag-gui 25, +6: dock round-trip x2, undock partition, empty-main, the Ctrl+Shift+Enter chord, per-window a11y) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is clean.

DATA proof: ShellCore::<TerminalViewer>::compute_paint_scene_for_window drives the REAL viewer's per-window paint — undocking pane 1 drops it from "main" and paints it alone in "pane-1"; dock-back re-tiles; all-floated yields an empty main without panic.

LIVE-verified (the R34 XTEST harness, ad-hoc): the real winit/GPU binary booted one window ("sprag terminal (interactive)"); a synthetic Ctrl+Shift+Enter opened a SECOND OS window ("sprag terminal — pane 0"), observed via xwininfo/Xlib; plus a boot-liveness smoke (no panic with the multi-window wiring).

Stop-and-report cleared for the FEATURE: multi-window is a public pinion seam (windows_signal/view_for_window; hello-dock-panels is the working precedent), and focus + the model scene are global (input is window-independent), so dock/undock of an existing pane does NOT hit PR-9 (it mints no new focusable tag).

Plan-agent pressure-test before the build; every load-bearing pinion fact source-verified (the two DEFAULT_WINDOW publish gates, the single global FocusManager, the view_for_window/windows_signal defaults, compute_paint_scene_for_window).
carry_forward_bullets: PR-10 reported (claudedocs/PINION-PR10-PER-WINDOW-VIEWPORT.md, separate doc): per-window viewport + pane-viewport publish (un-gate the DEFAULT_WINDOW check) unblocks RESIZABLE undock windows + undock-into-tiled-secondary. Until then undock windows are fixed-size (OS-resizable but non-reflowing) — the documented v1 bound. Stop-and-report; NO workaround (the fixed intrinsic size is a legitimate scope bound, not a hack).

Dynamic split/close + per-pane multi-tabs + DnD reorder remain gated on PR-9 (claudedocs/PINION-PR9-FOCUSABLE-REFRESH.md): runtime focusable refresh. Dock/undock side-stepped it (existing panes only).
Draggable splitter (pinion-widget-paint::view_splitter + SplitterExternal) is still available for the tiled layout when wanted.
Next can be the deferred adversarial session-review remediation (the R25/R30/R35 rhythm) over R36+R37, or a deferred axis once PR-9 / PR-10 land.

Round 38.decision_summary: Round 38: draggable splitter — drag the divider between tiled panes to resize them (was an even split), via pinion's view_splitter + SplitterExternal (pinion-widget-paint, GPU-free). N panes nest N-1 splitters with position-keyed ratio Signals. The interactive layout lives GUI-side (new split.rs) since it needs reactive ratios + a registered External the headless host has no use for; the host keeps the per-pane projection (pane_view_scene) and the now-dead workspace_view_scene even-tiling is removed. Reflow-on-drag is automatic (ratio set -> re-layout -> R1012 pane-rect publish -> per-pane reflow; the reflow seam was built for it). DATA-proven (ratio 0.7 -> panes reflow ~70/30) AND LIVE-verified (XTEST pointer drag on the handle -> PTYs resize 47/47 -> 66/28). No pinion edit.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui/split (new module): the draggable-divider layout. use_splitter_ratio(j) (Owner::cache-shared Rc<Signal<f32>>, default 0.5) + SPLITTER_TAGS (static, the &'static str discipline of PANE_TAGS) + view_split_row(panes, theme) (fold: 0 -> empty, 1 -> lone pane, N -> N-1 nested view_splitter, Horizontal, sized Percent(100) to fill compose). Ratios are POSITION-keyed (divider j = docked tile j vs everything to its right) — the proportional split-tree model.

sprag-gui/main: create_extra_externals registers MAX_PANES-1 SplitterExternals (Horizontal, attach_ratio(use_splitter_ratio(j))) sharing the view's ratio Signal — inert when a handle is not painted; the shell's pointer router drives the on-screen ones (NO WidgetCore pointer method). Splitter tags are NOT focusable (pointer-only). New pinion-widget-paint dep (GPU-free, already transitive via pinion-shell).
sprag-gui/view: view_main arranges the docked panes via split::view_split_row instead of the even host tiling; build_pane_scene + the dock floating filter are unchanged.

sprag-host: removed the now-dead workspace_view_scene + WORKSPACE_VIEW_TAG + PANE_GAP_PX + its test + the AlignItems/FlexDirection imports (no-dead-surface — only the GUI used it, and the GUI now owns the interactive arrangement). Kept pane_view_scene (the per-pane projection SSOT); doc honesty: the host projects each pane, the GUI arranges them.

No reflow.rs change: a drag mutates the ratio -> view re-renders -> compute_layout moves each pane_tag(i) rect -> R1012 publishes it -> the per-pane reflow Effect resizes the PTY; equality-skip bounds it to cell-boundary crossings (reflow.rs already named "a future splitter drags").

No pinion edit / no new PR: pinion's view_splitter + SplitterExternal seam (pinion-widget-paint) was sufficient and pointer dispatch to the External is automatic. The interactive layout lives GUI-side because it needs reactive ratios + a registered External the headless host has no use for (R25 satisfied: host owns per-pane projection, GUI owns the interactive arrangement).
verification_bullets: 159 workspace tests pass (sprag-gui 30, +5: split shape x3 + ratio round-trip + the divider-drag reweight; sprag-host -1 = the removed workspace_view_scene test) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is clean.

DATA proof: ShellCore::<TerminalViewer>::compute_paint_scene boots an even split, then setting divider 0's ratio to 0.7 (the exact write a pointer drag performs) re-weights the panes so the left pane reflows to ~70% (tracking 0.7 within tolerance) — the ratio -> layout -> R1012 reflow chain end-to-end.

LIVE-verified (the R37 XTEST harness extended with pointer events, ad-hoc): the real winit/GPU binary booted an even split (both panes 47 cols via stty size); a synthetic pointer drag of the handle to the 0.70 x-position (warp_pointer + ButtonPress/motion/ButtonRelease) reflowed the PTYs to 66/28 cols — the divider moved and the panes actually resized. Plus a boot-liveness smoke.
Split shape tests: 2 panes -> 1 divider handle, 3 -> 2 nested dividers, 1 -> none; the per-divider ratio Signals are independent and default even.

Plan-agent pressure-test before the build; load-bearing facts source-verified (view_splitter shape + apply_flex_main preserves the pane tag, SplitterExternal wants_pointer_capture + Gui backend + NO WidgetCore pointer method, pinion-widget-paint GPU-free + already transitive, the host-tiling-is-dead decision).
carry_forward_bullets: The divider ratios are POSITION-keyed, not pane-sticky: undock/dock re-compacts the docked set, so a remembered divider position then separates a different pane pair (the honest splitter-tree behavior; pane-identity-sticky ratios would need a real split-tree — premature at MAX_PANES=8). Nested splitters are proportional (divider j = tile j vs the rest), not independent columns.
Cosmetic gap (deferred, YAGNI): the handle does not visually brighten mid-drag (view_splitter dragging=false); the live highlight needs a per-splitter is_dragging mirror Signal.

Still gated on PR-9 (runtime focusable refresh) for dynamic split/close + per-pane tabs + DnD reorder + new-pane undock; PR-10 (per-window viewport publish) for resizable undock windows. Both reported as separate claudedocs docs.
Next can be the deferred adversarial session-review remediation (the R25/R30/R35 rhythm) over R36+R37+R38, or a deferred axis once PR-9 / PR-10 land.

Round 40.decision_summary: Round 40: GUI interaction round on sprag-gui — opt-in grid layout (SPRAG_GUI_LAYOUT=grid) reusing the view_splitter primitive (outer Vertical fold of rows, inner Horizontal fold of panes; grid_plan = the divider-id SSOT; row mode byte-unchanged); ADOPTED pinion R1020 scene-derived focus (pinion removed WidgetCore::focusable_tags(), so the pane Container is now with_focusable(true) and the shell derives the Tab order each frame via collect_focusable_tags — this resolved the long-deferred PR-9 and fixed the E0407 build break R1020 introduced); FIXED click-to-focus (the grid is tagged {pane}#grid so a press resolves through resolve_focusable to the focusable pane — the old shared GRID_TAG shadowed the pane so clicks never moved focus); added sprag-scoped rustfmt enforcement to the pre-commit hook (staged *.rs only, never cargo fmt --all which reaches pinion) plus formatted pre-existing drift. Live-verified in the real GPU window; reported 4 pinion gaps (PR-11..14), 2 delivered same-session (R1022/R1023). Pushed origin/main f45d03f + 85c3b8e.
changes_bullets: Grid layout (opt-in via SPRAG_GUI_LAYOUT=grid): N panes in a balanced 2D grid reusing the same view_splitter primitive — an outer Vertical fold of rows, each row an inner Horizontal fold of panes (split::view_grid over split::grid_plan). grid_plan(n) is the divider-id SSOT (column ids then row ids, gapless 0..n-1) so the view fold and the boot External registration agree on count + orientation. Row mode (default) is byte-unchanged; grid holds a floated pane's slot as an untagged empty cell rather than compacting (boot-only Externals weld each divider's drag-axis).

Adopted pinion R1020 scene-derived focus: pinion removed WidgetCore::focusable_tags(), so sprag-host pane_view_scene now marks the pane Container with_focusable(true) (the splitter apply_flex_main / fill map_layout preserve the flag) and the shell derives the Tab order each frame from Scene::collect_focusable_tags. Dropped sprag-gui's focusable_tags() (the E0407 build break R1020 caused) and updated terminal.rs/split.rs docs. This is the resolution of the long-deferred PR-9 (runtime focusable refresh).

Fixed click-to-focus: pane_view_scene tags the grid {pane}#grid (a composite sub-tag) instead of the shared GRID_TAG, so a pointer press on the grid (the deepest tagged node) resolves through pinion resolve_focusable / composite_tag::split_subindex to the focusable pane. The old shared GRID_TAG shadowed the pane (resolve returned None -> clicks never moved focus) and was ambiguous across panes; grid_node now takes the tag (the headless data path keeps GRID_TAG).

Added sprag-scoped rustfmt enforcement: .githooks/pre-commit now runs rustfmt --check on the staged *.rs files (edition 2024). Staged-scoped BY CONSTRUCTION so it never reaches pinion path-deps — unlike cargo fmt --all, which walks into pinion (forbidden by the never-touch-pinion rule). Formatted pre-existing rustfmt drift across all sprag crates.
Added pinion-runtime as a sprag-gui DEV-dependency for PointerId (the e2e click-to-focus test drives the real shell pointer path); no sprag crate depends on pinion-runtime at runtime.
verification_bullets: sprag-gui 42 tests + sprag-host 38 tests pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New tests: panes_are_scene_derived_focus_stops (collect_focusable_tags == both pane tags, root/splitter excluded), boot_focus_lands_on_pane_zero (after finalize_frame, focused == pane_tag(0)), clicking_a_pane_focuses_it (cursor_moved -> mouse_pressed -> click_to_focus moves focus to the clicked pane); the host pane_view_scene test asserts the {pane}#grid composite splits back to the pane.

Click-to-focus bug reproduced as DATA first (clicking pane 1 left focused on sprag_gui.pane.0), then the composite-tag fix made the same e2e test pass — the live "clicking the right pane kept typing in the left" symptom.

Live-verified in the real GPU window (DISPLAY=:0, WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1): the R1020 migration restored boot focus + typing (focused == pane 0 via the boot focus_request drain). A fresh build against pinion R1022 (PR-11 focus-ring far-edge clamp) + R1023 (PR-12 winit Resized requests a redraw) cleared the focus-ring edge clipping and the resize-clear ghosting the earlier stale binary showed.

The new rustfmt hook fired on the actual commit (pre-commit: rustfmt --check (staged *.rs) passed); both commits pushed to origin/main (22abe6b..85c3b8e: f45d03f the round, 85c3b8e the fmt gate) through the pre-push mnemosyne validate + clippy gates.
carry_forward_bullets: Reported to pinion (not yet delivered): PR-13 (click_to_focus_for_window changes focus but does NOT request a redraw -> the focus ring lags until the next event; the programmatic drain_focus_request path DOES) and PR-14 (ShellCore exposes no pointer hover/capture READ accessor, unlike focus()/redraw_requested() -> no grounded test for pointer-driven interaction). claudedocs PINION-PR13/PR14.

Open: the splitter (divider) drag does not re-weight the panes via the ShellCore pointer path (ratio stays 0.5 after press+drag); cannot pinpoint hover vs capture vs pointer_move without PR-14's read accessors. Prime suspect is the 4px handle (handle_extent_px) being too thin to hit on a 2x HiDPI display — a candidate sprag-side UX fix is widening it.

pinion DELIVERED this session: PR-9 (R1020 scene-derived focus, adopted here), PR-10 (R1021 per-window pane-viewport publish), PR-11 (R1022 focus-ring far-edge framebuffer clamp), PR-12 (R1023 winit Resized requests a redraw). Resizable undock (the PR-10 consumer) is now unblocked but unwired.

Ground rule cemented in memory: the instant pinion/SCE needs support -> immediately STOP + write a claudedocs PINION-PRn doc (+ index in PINION-REQUIREMENTS) + report; never edit pinion source from a sprag session (read-to-diagnose only). pinion builds: cargo build -j 4 -p <crate>, never --all/full (it reaches pinion path-deps).

Round 41.decision_summary: Round 41: paint-only per-pane vertical scrollbar (gnome-terminal style) on sprag-gui — a pure projection of use_scroll_offset (the row authority) via pinion's unit-agnostic scrollbar_thumb_rect driven in ROWS; no ScrollState/mirror/drag (one authority). Track height from R1012 use_pane_viewport_size (the winsize SSOT). The bar is a sibling of the focusable pane grid; the grid loses the gutter. Drag deferred to pinion PR-16 (ScrollBarExternal lacks a caller-owned drag authority like SplitterExternal::attach_ratio). Committed 7649224 on main.
changes_bullets: New crates/sprag-gui/src/scrollbar.rs: view_pane_scrollbar builds a track Container (tag scrollbar_tag(i), SurfaceContainerHighest) + a thumb Box (Outline, corner radius) absolutely positioned from pinion's unit-agnostic scrollbar_thumb_rect driven in ROWS (viewport=visible_rows, content=visible_rows+scrollback_len, scroll_offset=scrollback_len-rows = the inversion: rows=0 live -> thumb at the bottom). No ScrollState, no mirror, no cell_h.

wrap_pane_with_bar pairs the pane grid with its bar in an untagged horizontal flex Row [grid (flex-grow 1, flex-basis 0), bar (fixed GUTTER_W=8)]; the grid keeps pane_tag(i) as the sole R1012-measured + focusable node, so cols shrink by the gutter (the gnome-terminal width) and the bar is a sibling, never a wrapper that steals the tag.

view::build_pane_scene reads the track height from use_pane_viewport_size(pane_tag(i)).1 (the winsize SSOT) and (grid, scrollback_len, visible_rows) from with_screen, then wraps. SCROLLBAR_TAGS[MAX_PANES], pointer-only (never with_focusable), so the bar stays out of R1020's scene-derived Tab order.
verification_bullets: sprag-gui tests pass (7 new scrollbar tests: thumb at the bottom when live, at the top at oldest, full track with no history, wrap preserves pane_tag) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is clean.

Live-verified in the real GPU window: the bar renders to the right of each pane and the thumb tracks keyboard scroll (Shift+PageUp/Down) for free, because it is a function of the same use_scroll_offset the chord writes.
carry_forward_bullets: DRAG deferred to pinion PR-16 (claudedocs/PINION-PR16-SCROLLBAR-DRAG-AUTHORITY.md): ScrollBarExternal hard-wires writing a px ScrollState (reads state.offset for the press snapshot AND writes on drag), so wiring it to the row authority would force a bidirectional mirror+echo, the codebase's first dual-source-of-truth. SplitterExternal::attach_ratio has no such problem; the asymmetry is the reported gap.

Round 42.decision_summary: Round 42: debounce the TIOCSWINSZ resize storm in sprag-terminal — a continuous splitter/window drag fired one TIOCSWINSZ (and thus one SIGWINCH -> shell prompt redraw) per cell-width boundary. A per-session coalescer thread now owns the PTY master and debounces the ioctl to the FINAL size (40ms quiet window, last-write-wins, flush on Drop). The emulator resize stays SYNCHRONOUS so the GUI's same-frame reflow is preserved. This is the A half of the resize-stale fix (B = Round 43 emulator rewrap). Committed 964789c on main.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-terminal/src/session.rs: TerminalSession drops the stored master; spawn_with_dirty moves the master into a sprag-pty-resize thread running run_resize_coalescer (mpsc recv_timeout: store the latest pending on Ok, apply pending on Timeout, flush+break on Disconnected). resize(&self) calls emulator.resize synchronously (same-frame reflow) then sends (cols,rows) to the channel; Drop drops the sender and joins the thread.

run_resize_coalescer is generic over the apply closure (master.resize(PtySize)) for testability. The debounce is TIOCSWINSZ-only — moving the emulator resize off-thread broke the GUI's same-frame reflow tests, so it stays synchronous.
workspace.rs resize_updates_dimensions test reverted to a synchronous assert (the emulator resize is synchronous; only the ioctl is debounced).

Round 43.decision_summary: Round 43: reflow the screen on resize (the COMPLETE resize-stale fix). A per-row wrapped flag (DEC LINE_WRAPPED), set at the autowrap site and cleared on a hard LF / erase-to-margin, lets Screen::reflowed reconstruct logical lines (rows joined by the flag), re-break them at the new width (cursor preserved by logical position, wide-cluster-safe, alt screen verbatim), and bottom-anchor with overflow scrolling into scrollback. Emulator::resize calls reflowed for the Main screen. Committed fc22d64 on main.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-vt/src/port.rs: Screen gains wrapped: Vec<bool> (threaded through new/clear_row/resized/scroll_up), set_wrapped/wrapped accessors, and Screen::reflowed(cols, rows, generation): pass 1 reconstructs logical lines from glyph cells (trailers dropped, trailing blanks trimmed at hard ends, trailing empty lines dropped), pass 2 re-breaks each at the new width (a wide cluster moves whole), pass 3 materializes bottom-anchored with overflow scrolling into scrollback. Alt/degenerate falls back to the verbatim resized().

crates/sprag-vt/src/emulator.rs: print_str sets the wrapped flag at the autowrap (col+cell_w > cols); control LineFeed and erase-to-margin clear it. Emulator::resize calls reflowed (a fresh generation stamps every re-laid-out row) for both the active and saved-main screens, adopting the cursor reflowed re-derives.

Round 44.decision_summary: Round 44: a headless regression guard for the resize-stale accumulation bug — a real-bash-PTY harness in sprag-terminal that reproduces the OPEN bug (a rapid resize of a wrapping prompt makes the emulator stack bash's readline redisplay; full_text accumulates ~44 prompts). Corrects this session's earlier over-claims that R42/R43 fixed it — they are PARTIAL, the bug is open. RED extreme guard is #[ignore]d (un-ignore when the emulator handles the narrow-width redisplay); a GREEN no-wrap guard runs in CI. Committed 937d7c6 on main.
changes_bullets: New crates/sprag-terminal/tests/resize_accumulation.rs — a reusable headless harness (bash_session spawns /bin/bash --norc -i with a 40-col PS1; settle polls the screen's max row-generation until quiet, since bash's redraw is async; drag_sweep/drag_widths drive a rapid resize sweep; prompt_count reads Screen::full_text) plus two guards that drive a real PTY (the headless equivalent of a splitter drag).

rapid_extreme_resize_does_not_accumulate_prompts (RED, #[ignore]d): a rapid sweep to ~4 cols and back asserts <= 3 prompts but gets 44 — reproduces the open bug. Three load-bearing conditions, each of which alone hides it: a prompt that WRAPS to many rows, a step gap ABOVE R42's ~40ms debounce (so each step delivers its own SIGWINCH — below it the coalescer merges to one resize), and an extreme-narrow width.

rapid_resize_without_wrapping_stays_clean (GREEN, runs in CI): the same storm above the wrap width stays clean — isolating the multi-row redisplay (not the storm count, not PTY/emulator desync) as the trigger.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p sprag-terminal: 9 pass + 1 ignored; the GREEN guard passes, the RED guard (cargo test -p sprag-terminal -- --ignored) fails with "a RAPID extreme resize accumulated 44 prompts". cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is clean; rustfmt clean.

The harness is pure TerminalSession (no GUI / no renderer) and still reproduces the accumulation, confirming it is REAL emulator producer state (full_text), not GPU paint — pinning the layer the fix targets.
carry_forward_bullets: THE RESIZE-STALE BUG IS OPEN — this round corrects this session's earlier over-claims that R42/R43 "fixed it" (they are PARTIAL). Root cause: the emulator (a walking-skeleton VT subset, no scroll-region / IL-DL) does not overwrite bash/readline's multi-row prompt redisplay at narrow widths during a SIGWINCH storm. NOT desync (at >40ms/step the PTY flushes per step so bash and the emulator agree on width, yet it still accumulates), NOT only GPU paint. R43 reflow reduces a SETTLED extreme resize to ~6; the storm leaves ~44.

NEXT-SESSION FIX (methodical, not blind constant-tweaking): capture bash's narrow-width SIGWINCH redraw bytes (a standalone python pty running bash, resize narrow, read its output — no sprag temp files), identify the mishandled cursor/erase/scroll sequence, implement it in sprag-vt/src/emulator.rs, then UN-IGNORE the RED guard when it goes green.

Separately delivered/open: pinion R1028 (PR-15, TextGrid pass-0 default-bg gutter fill) fixed the WHITE SLACK BAR (a distinct real issue); pinion PR-16 (ScrollBarExternal caller-owned drag authority for the scrollbar drag) is open. Capture lesson: GPU-window PIXEL truth needs root.get_image / ffmpeg x11grab, not win.get_image (which hid the accumulation all session); raising the window triggers a repaint that clears it.

Round 45.decision_summary: Round 45: FIX the resize-stale accumulation bug (open since R42-R44). Root cause: the R43 reflow anchored the cursor at the rewrapped line's BOTTOM row, but a live shell's SIGWINCH redraw (CR + erase-in-line + reprint, no cursor-up) rewrites from the prompt's TOP row, so each per-width redraw stacked below the last (full_text grew to 44 prompts). Fix: Screen::reflowed anchors the cursor to its logical line's FIRST physical row (column preserved). The R44 RED guard now passes against real bash and is un-ignored as the permanent regression guard. Committed 1ed02ac on main.
changes_bullets: sprag-vt/src/port.rs Screen::reflowed: Pass 2 now tracks cursor_line_top (the first physical row of the cursor's logical line); Pass 3 sets the cursor row to it instead of the row the glyph offset lands on. The column is preserved — a line editor's CR resets it, and for a single-row line the top IS the cursor's own row (so reflow_rejoins is unchanged). Doc comment updated; only the cursor's row contract changed.

Root cause, captured as DATA from real bash (standalone python pty, no sprag temp files): bash's SIGWINCH redraw is CR + erase-in-line + reprint with NO cursor-up in the gradual case; readline believes the cursor is at the prompt top but an autowrapping reprint physically left it at the bottom. A reflow that anchors the cursor at the logical END desyncs this, so CR lands mid-line and the reprint stacks BELOW the old text.

Updated reflow_rebreaks_a_line_when_narrowed (cursor row 1 -> 0, column kept) and added reflow_anchors_cursor_to_logical_line_top; un-ignored rapid_extreme_resize_does_not_accumulate_prompts (the R44 RED guard) so it is now the permanent regression guard.

Fix direction validated first on a DETERMINISTIC replay: a captured real-bash resize sweep (the exact CR+EL+reprint protocol) replayed straight through Emulator accumulated 44 prompts before the fix and exactly 1 after — no PTY/timing. Mechanism cross-checked against a faithful non-reflow reference model and pyte (both also accumulate, proving the bytes accumulate in any naive emulator and the cursor anchor is the fix).

The fix is a cursor-anchor in Screen::reflowed, not a new VT sequence — bash uses only CR/EL/CUU/print, all already handled; the emulator's reflow cursor placement was the gap.

Known minor cosmetic (not a bug): after a resize and before bash's redraw lands, the cursor sits at the prompt's top row for one frame (snaps back when bash repaints). Far better than stacked prompts and unavoidable without reintroducing the bug (the same cursor serves both rendering and the redraw target).

Round 46.decision_summary: Round 46: follow-up to R45 — the cursor-column half of the resize-stale fix. R45 anchored the reflow cursor's ROW to its logical line's top but kept the natural COLUMN (offset-mod-width), so during a live splitter drag the painted caret skated left/right across the prompt's first row (user-reported, RPC-confirmed). Fix: pin the column to 0 when the cursor is pulled above its natural physical row; keep the natural (col,row) when it already sits on the top row. Committed 400f57e on main.
changes_bullets: sprag-vt/src/port.rs Screen::reflowed Pass 3: when the cursor's natural physical row (cphys) differs from its logical line's first row (cursor_line_top) it has been pulled up, so pin the column to 0; otherwise keep the natural (col, row). The row anchor (the R45 accumulation fix) is unchanged.

Root cause: offset-mod-width is the cursor's column on the BOTTOM row (where it marks the prompt end); placing that column on the TOP row makes it slide as a multi-row line re-breaks at different widths. Column 0 is width-independent, so a still caret reads as stable, not jumping; the line editor's CR resets the column on its next redraw anyway.
Updated reflow_rebreaks_a_line_when_narrowed (cursor 2,0 to 0,0) and added reflow_keeps_natural_column_on_a_single_row_line (a 1-row line keeps the caret after the text, column intact).

Round 47.decision_summary: Round 47: the typed-input half of the resize-stale fix. R45/R46 fixed the EMPTY-prompt accumulation, but with typed input on the command line a rapid resize still stacked dozens of ghost prompts. Root cause (captured from real bash AND gnome-terminal via a PTY proxy): at a width the wrapped prompt+input exactly fills, readline redraws it with an explicit CR LF instead of relying on autowrap, and sprag treated that as a hard line break, so each per-width copy became a separate logical line that could not rejoin on a later widen. vte/gnome-terminal keep it soft and collapse it. Fix: within the resize-redraw window, treat the editor's CR LF as a soft wrap and extend its erase-in-line over the whole wrapped active line. Committed e5c0d9a on main.
changes_bullets: sprag-vt/src/emulator.rs: new in_resize_redraw flag, set on resize() for the MAIN screen and cleared after the next advance() batch (the line editor's SIGWINCH redraw). Reinterprets two actions only within that window.

control() LineFeed: set_wrapped(row, in_resize_redraw). A CR LF inside the editor's resize redraw is a soft wrap (keeps the redraw one logical line that collapses on a later widen); a hard break otherwise, so ordinary command output keeps its real newlines.

edit() EraseInLine-to-end-of-line during the redraw also clears the active line's soft-wrapped continuation rows (walk the wrap chain to its last row FIRST, since clear_row drops the flag), so the prior width's stale input tail does not survive as a leftover.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p sprag-vt: 32 pass (4 new: redraw CR LF is soft, normal CR LF is hard, the window ends after one batch, the redraw erase clears the wrapped continuation). 4 real-bash integration guards pass (empty long prompt, ASCII echo-hi, Korean wide-char input, non-wrapping). clippy + rustfmt clean.

Root cause and target confirmed by capturing bash's bytes through gnome-terminal with a PTY proxy (forks bash, propagates SIGWINCH, tees output): bash sends an explicit CR LF at exact-fill widths; gnome-terminal/vte stay clean by collapsing it, sprag R46 stacked 16-44 ghost prompts. Headless sweep with the user's long prompt + input dropped from 16 to 1.

Live GUI via JSON-RPC: scene/drag the splitter (handle = sprag_gui.split.0 children[1].rect, re-fetched each drag since it moves) to narrow then widen pane.1; the prompt count stayed 1 per pane with no stacking.
carry_forward_bullets: Remaining debt: a wide-char (Korean) line at certain narrow widths still shows bash's own CR LF break (one input syllable on the prompt row, the rest on the next). Confirmed identical in R46 AND in gnome-terminal via the PTY proxy, so it is bash behavior, not a sprag regression; left as-is rather than risk re-introducing the reflow-vs-editor desync by collapsing the active line.

Never guess pixel coordinates: the handle gap sits past scrollbar.0, not at the naive pane-midpoint (x=480 not x=476 at boot).

Round 48.decision_summary: Round 48: adversarial session-review remediation of R47 (the R30/R35/R39 rhythm — a refactoring lens + an architecture lens + my SSOT/source cross-check). Verdict: R47's mechanism is sound and correctly placed (producer-side per §3, no pinion contamination) but not-yet-textbook. Cleared 1 must-fix + majors + minors: the redraw continuation-clear is now one atomic invariant-safe Screen method (was a mutate-while-iterating reconstruction across the Emulator/Screen boundary), gated to EraseToEndOfLine, with the soft-wrap decision named and the wrapped-flag SSOT doc corrected to name both writers. KEY: my cross-check OVERTURNED the architecture lens's proposed pure-structural alternative — bash's CR LF lands mid-row (premature, byte-indistinguishable from a hard newline), so the redraw CONTEXT is necessary, not a workaround. Committed 6ff63fe on main.
changes_bullets: sprag-vt/src/port.rs: new Screen::clear_soft_wrap_continuation(row, gen) — one atomic, invariant-safe op that walks the wrap chain to its last row BEFORE clearing (clear_row drops the flag). Replaces the two-if reconstruction the emulator did across the Emulator/Screen boundary (the session review's must-fix: a mutate-while-iterating ordering hazard that left the soft-wrap SSOT internally inconsistent for a mid-chain erase).

sprag-vt/src/emulator.rs edit(): the redraw continuation-clear is now gated to matches!(mode, EraseToEndOfLine) (the readline idiom) instead of the end>=cols proxy that also caught EraseLine (\x1b[2K); it calls the new Screen method. control() LineFeed reads a named `soft_wrap` local instead of passing in_resize_redraw positionally into set_wrapped.

sprag-vt/src/port.rs wrapped-field doc now names BOTH writers (autowrap site + the resize-redraw LineFeed) and states the second is a deliberate, context-only decision; emulator in_resize_redraw doc adds WHY-a-window (the editor CR LF lands mid-row, byte-indistinguishable from a hard newline) and honest scope LIMITS (first/single advance batch). Per-call comments deduped to point at the field doc.

crates/sprag-terminal/tests/resize_accumulation.rs: drag_sweep and drag_sweep_with_input unified into one drag_sweep(input) (empty input = bare-prompt path); header updated to four guards; the Korean guard's docstring made honest (a wide-char real-bash smoke complementing the char-agnostic unit tests).
verification_bullets: No behavior change (a remediation): 32 sprag-vt unit tests, the 4 real-bash integration guards (bare prompt, ASCII echo-hi, Korean wide-char, non-wrapping), sprag-host 38 tests all pass; sprag-gui builds; clippy and rustfmt clean.

My SSOT/source cross-check OVERTURNED the architecture lens's proposed alternative: it argued for a pure structural pending-wrap latch (no mode, no editor knowledge). Verified from the captured bytes that bash's CR LF lands at col 13 of a 20-wide row — a PREMATURE mid-row break, byte-for-byte identical to a genuine newline; no margin/pending-wrap rule can distinguish it. Only the redraw CONTEXT marks it soft (vte/gnome-terminal likewise rely on context and also show the break until widen). So the redraw-window mechanism is NECESSARY, not a workaround; the smell was the implementation, now cleared.
carry_forward_bullets: The in_resize_redraw window's scope limits are now documented honestly rather than hardened: it assumes the editor's redraw is the first advance batch after the resize and fits in one PTY read. This holds for real editor prompt redraws (small, foreground); widening the scope (e.g. arming on the CR + erase-in-line signature) is deferred until a case is observed to need it.

The wide-char (Korean) IMMEDIATE break at narrow widths remains: bash's own premature CR LF puts the continuation on a new row; gnome-terminal/vte show it identically (confirmed via a PTY-proxy byte capture). Collapsing it immediately would require reflowing the active line, which reintroduces the editor/reflow cursor desync R45/R46 fixed — so it is left as faithful rendering (it collapses on widen via the R47 soft wrap).

Round 49.decision_summary: Round 49: the per-pane vertical scrollbar reworked onto pinion ScrollState as the SINGLE scroll authority (replacing the R16-era paint-only Signal<usize> projection) — drag enabled via the now-delivered R1032/PR-16 caller-owned-ScrollState seam, a higher-contrast thumb, and an offset_lines projection DERIVED (not stored) from the one authority. A follow-up wheel/touchpad attempt was caught by a 2-lens adversarial session review as an R1.7 layer violation (a GUI ScrollState + External::wheel injected into the AI-facing SpragPaneExternal) and REVERTED; the wheel and two adjacent gaps are reported as pinion PR-18/19/20, and reconcile_scroll was collapsed onto pinion follow_tail. Committed c6015d5 (scrollbar) + b5b6f7d (review remediation) on main.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui/src/scrollbar.rs: scroll authority is now the per-pane pinion ScrollState (use_pane_scroll); offset_lines_from_top (= scrollback_len - offset_y) DERIVES the projection offset each frame with no stored mirror; the bar reads offset_y + use_scrollbar_interaction and paints a higher-contrast thumb (OnSurfaceMuted idle / OnSurface hover-drag) over the SurfaceContainerHighest track via the row-unit scrollbar_thumb_rect geometry primitive (pinion's sanctioned row-unit consumer per R1032).

Drag delivered per pane via scrollbar_extra_external (the R1032/PR-16 caller-owned ScrollState seam); the old Signal<usize> use_scroll_offset is deleted; input.rs chords (page_delta -> scroll_by; typing/IME snap -> scroll_to(max)) and view.rs projection migrated to the one ScrollState; reconcile_scroll delegates to pinion follow_tail (row_pitch 1, viewport 0) instead of a hand-rolled set_max/scroll_to.

Wheel/touchpad scroll attempt REVERTED after the session review: it had put a GUI ScrollState + an External::wheel impl onto the AI-facing SpragPaneExternal (sprag-host), violating R1.7 ('the engine carries no scene state'). Three pinion gaps reported as claudedocs handoffs + REQUIREMENTS index: PR-18 (GUI-side wheel seam, e.g. WidgetCore::apply_wheel), PR-19 (view_vertical_scrollbar idle-thumb fill override), PR-20 (scroll-bound reducer for non-Scene::Scroll offset-projecting consumers).
verification_bullets: 55 sprag-gui + 38 sprag-host unit/integration tests pass (incl. the real-viewer painted-track assertion, the thumb-vs-track contrast color assertion, offset->thumb monotonicity, and reconcile follow/hold); clippy and rustfmt clean; both commits' pre-commit workspace-clippy + validate-workspace gates passed.

Live (hidden-window, in-process JSON-RPC): contrast confirmed (track RGB(230,224,233) vs thumb RGB(96,96,96) - distinct); drag confirmed by a SEMANTIC thumb-center scene/drag moving both panes' thumbs (563->375) through the SAME cursor_moved/mouse_pressed core path real winit mouse drives (pinion-shell lib.rs: all input drains converge at mouse_pressed_for_window); the reverted wheel was itself live-verified (scene/wheel over the grid scrolled the thumb) before revert, proving the gap is wiring/layer-placement, not logic.
carry_forward_bullets: Wheel/touchpad scroll is NOT shipped: the AI-facing pane engine 'carries no scene state' (R1.7) and pinion's scene/wheel drives the same router as a real wheel, so an RPC scene/wheel would scroll the human's GUI viewport if the ScrollState lived on SpragPaneExternal. Awaits pinion PR-18 (a GUI-side wheel seam), exactly as drag awaited R1032/PR-16. Scroll today = drag + Shift+PageUp/Down.

Reported pinion gaps (claudedocs/PINION-PR18..20 + REQUIREMENTS status-update 13): PR-18 GUI wheel sink; PR-19 view_vertical_scrollbar idle-thumb fill override (so sprag's hand-painted thumb can collapse back to view_vertical_scrollbar); PR-20 a scroll-bound reducer for offset-projecting non-Scroll consumers - reconcile_scroll currently runs follow_tail in the pure view-fn (loop-safe via Signal equality-skip but a seam smell, since update_scroll_state_bounds only reconciles Scene::Scroll nodes and the terminal grid is a Scene::TextGrid).

Session-review verdict (2 independent lenses + SSOT cross-check): committed R49 is textbook (single ScrollState SSOT, derived offset_lines, substrate drag). Two cross-check CORRECTIONS recorded: (1) reconcile can NOT trivially move to an Effect (scrollback_len is non-reactive and the producer is off-thread, so no dep to subscribe) -> it is a substrate-integration gap, PR-20; (2) hand-painting the thumb is NOT a substrate violation (R1032 explicitly names sprag the row-unit consumer of scrollbar_thumb_rect) - only the idle-fill override is the gap, PR-19.

Drag UX caveat (not a bug): the 8px scrollbar track is a narrow pointer target and pane 0's sits immediately left of the splitter handle (scrollbar x 470-478, splitter ~478-482), so a real mouse/touchpad easily misses it; pane 1's far-right bar is unambiguous. The wheel (PR-18) would moot precise thumb-grabbing. No X11 input-injection tooling (xdotool/xte/uinput) was available to drive the literal mouse, so drag was verified via the convergent RPC pointer path.

Round 5.decision_summary: Restructure into producer/projection/host layers and harden the headless host: honest winsize, bounded state, enforced read-only.
changes_bullets: New sprag-host crate (scene assembly + snapshot + RPC server + sprag-term bin); pinion-rpc and its heavy transitive deps confined there (S1)
sprag-terminal reduced to a pure PTY producer with no pinion dependency; reader thread applies bytes to a Mutex<Emulator> (bounded state, no caller pump) (S3)
Headless winsize made honest: scene() leaves the GUI rect unset, authoritative dims are the GridBuffer buffer_cols/rows; supersedes the now-inaccurate R3 §3 caveat (S2)
RPC host enforces a read-only method allowlist, returning -32601 for the rest; removes the silent-mutation-success smell (S4)
verification_bullets: 21 tests pass (sprag-vt 10, sprag-grid 4, sprag-terminal 1, sprag-host 6); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean
Bin end-to-end: live snapshot reports buffer_cols/rows authoritative with cols/rows=0; scene/key rejected with -32601

Round 52.decision_summary: Round 52: remediated the R50/R51 adversarial session review (two independent lenses: refactoring + architecture). Both flagged that R51's PaneSlot was advertised as "the per-pane identity SSOT" while three more per-pane keys (preedit/reflow/wheel_accum) were minted by separate format! calls outside it. Fixed by (a) narrowing PaneSlot's doc to its true scope (the &'static External-tag identity) and (b) a single pane_cache_key(ns,i) mint site that preedit/reflow/wheel_accum now share. Also: the wheel accumulator discards its sub-row remainder when ScrollState::scroll_by clamps at a boundary (no stale wrong-side fraction on reversal); the alignment test asserts full strings + covers pane_cache_key; multi-window caveats documented on reconcile_frame + apply_wheel; the broken PANE_TAGS link + the rest of sprag-gui's intra-doc links cleaned (cargo doc 0 warnings). The architecture lens OVERTURNED the refactoring lens's "terminal.rs owning scrollbar/scroll naming is a layer smell" — terminal.rs is the correct home (per-pane identity is the terminal model's concern; clean dependency direction). Committed 7fac232 on main.
changes_bullets: terminal.rs: PANE_SLOTS doc narrowed to the &'static External-tag identity SSOT (was over-claimed as the whole per-pane identity); new pane_cache_key(namespace, index) is the ONE site that mints per-pane Owner::cache keys.
input.rs preedit_key / reflow.rs reflow_key / scrollbar.rs wheel_accum now call pane_cache_key (was three separate format! sites) so the index suffix is derived in one place.

scrollbar.rs wheel_scroll_pane reads ScrollState::offset_y before/after scroll_by and discards the accumulator remainder when the offset is unchanged (clamped boundary), so a reversal never starts with a stale wrong-side fraction.

terminal.rs test pane_slot_tags_match_their_namespace_and_index asserts each tag is EXACTLY sprag_gui.<ns>.<i> (catches a prefix typo / duplicated row that a suffix-only check missed) and checks pane_cache_key.

Round 55.decision_summary: Round 55: wired resizable undock — the undock window now reflows its pane to its own size in both axes (consuming pinion R1021's per-window pane-viewport publish, PINION-PR10 delivered), fixed by giving the lone-pane scene a definite extent via fill_definite; reported the remaining shrink-floor as PINION-PR23.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui view::view_for_window undock branch now wraps the lone pane in split::fill_definite (made pub(crate)) — the same definite Percent(100) extent the docked arrangements (view_split_row / view_grid) apply as their final step. Without it the undock pane filled the window width (cross-axis stretch) but its height collapsed to the grid's content rows (the sizeless flex main axis), so the window reflowed only horizontally; with it the pane reflows to its window in BOTH axes.

No new wiring was needed for the reflow itself: the existing per-pane reflow Effect (subscribing use_pane_viewport_size(pane_tag(i))) already fires for an undock window because pinion R1021 publishes per-pane viewport rects for EVERY painted window, not just DEFAULT_WINDOW — PINION-PR10 delivered. The R1006 window-size seam (use_viewport_size) stays primary-gated, but undock needs only the per-pane publish.

Updated the stale docs that predated R1021: crate-root main.rs and dock.rs module docs claimed the undock window opens fixed-size and does NOT reflow on OS resize (a pinion gap) — now they describe both-axis reflow via R1021, plus the remaining shrink-floor bound. Refined the toggle_pane_floating / cell_px comments (fits 1:1 at tear-off, then reflows).

Reported the remaining bound as a new pinion requirement PINION-PR23-RESIZABLE-WINDOW-MIN-FLOOR: SizeStrategy::Fixed floors winit min_inner_size at the open size, so the undock window can grow (and reflow) but cannot shrink below its intrinsic size, and no SizeStrategy decouples open-size from min-floor (Fixed couples them; IntrinsicAfterFirstPaint opens at min and the fill content has no intrinsic bbox). Shipped Fixed as the named bound (no workaround). Updated PINION-REQUIREMENTS index (+PR-23 row) and the PINION-PR10 doc status to delivered+consumed with a consumption note.
verification_bullets: 57 sprag-gui tests pass (new undock_window_reflows_its_pane_to_its_own_size guard + the existing docked tiles_two_panes / focus / dock tests); cargo clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -p sprag-gui with RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings --document-private-items 0 warnings.

Root cause isolated by a headless probe: the docked main window already reflows vertically (960x360 -> 12 rows, 960x900 -> 30 rows) but the undock window's pane rect kept h=600/900 (the grid content height) while honoring width — pinpointing a missing definite extent (fill_definite), a sprag-side layout bug, NOT a pinion gap. The reflow mechanism is direction-agnostic (the guard drives two sizes and asserts both grow and shrink in the paint path); only the live winit min-floor (PR-23) blocks user shrink.

Built sprag-gui against the git-pinned pinion (rev 0cc79f78, R1053) and read the two load-bearing facts directly: publish_pane_viewports is per-window (R1021, not DEFAULT_WINDOW-gated) and SizeStrategy::Fixed sets with_min_inner_size = the open size (pinion-shell app.rs).
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR23 (resizable-window min-floor): deliver a SizeStrategy that opens at a chosen size with a lower min floor, then make the undock window (and the main window, also Fixed) freely shrinkable; until then Fixed is the named bound (grow-reflows, no shrink).

Live GUI confirmation of undock resize-reflow is optional — the deterministic headless guard is the cemented faithful gate, and the winit min-floor means live shrink cannot be exercised until PR-23 lands anyway.

Round 58.decision_summary: Round 58: scrollback now preserves cell colors/attributes — stores styled cells (VecDeque<Vec<Cell>>) instead of plain text, so scrolled-back history paints in its original colors (the user saw scrolled-back prompts as plain while the live prompt was green); the AI-facing text path is unchanged (derived from the cells).
changes_bullets: sprag-vt port.rs: scrollback storage changed from VecDeque<String> (plain text) to VecDeque<Vec<Cell>> (styled cells — fg/bg/attrs/width preserved). The scroll_up (line-feed) and reflow push sites now store the row's styled cells instead of flattening to text; a new cells_text() free fn is the single row-to-text SSOT that row_text/scrollback_rows/full_text all derive through, so the AI-facing text path (full_text, scrollback_len) is byte-unchanged. New scrollback_cells() accessor feeds the grid; scrollback_rows() now yields owned text derived from the cells; row_cells() captures a row for scroll-off.

sprag-grid lib.rs: history_row(&str) -> project_glyph_row(&[Cell]) — renders scrolled-back rows through the same term_cell mapping as the live grid (color/attrs), synthesizing the head+trailer pair for wide heads and SKIPPING any stored trailer, so a row stored with trailers (scroll-off path) and one without (reflow path) render identically. project_scrolled reads scrollback_cells().
Root cause of the user report (scrolled-back prompt plain while live prompt green): scrollback was text-only, so history rows projected with default fg/bg. Now they keep their colors.

Round 60.decision_summary: Round 60: replaced the flat row/grid pane layout (position-keyed dividers + grid hold-slots) with a pinion DockTopology split-tree — the identity-keyed canonical shape the old split.rs docs deferred to, now reachable via pinion R689 external_set_is_dynamic. The docked panes are a held Signal<Option<DockTopology>>; undock collapses the leaf so the rest reclaim its space and dock-back re-inserts in left-to-right index order; each pane gains pinion's 28px view_dock_panel header (the drag handle P2 drag-dock and P3 tear-off will use). Foundation phase (P1) of the user-approved drag-and-drop dock migration; the user chose collapse-on-undock + adopt-the-header.
changes_bullets: split.rs rewritten from the flat model (SPLITTER_TAGS / grid_plan / LayoutMode / view_split_row / view_grid / divider_orientations, ~800 lines) to the dock-tree model: use_dock_topology() holds Signal<Option<DockTopology>> seeded with a right-nested all-horizontal boot tree (byte-identical to the old row default at any pane count, None when no panes are docked); panel_id(i)="terminal-{i}" maps 1:1 to the tile via pane_index_of_panel; use_split_ratio(id, initial) is the per-Split ratio Signal shared with the drag SplitterExternal; float_pane(i) removes the leaf (RootRemoval -> None when the last docked pane floats), dock_pane(i) re-inserts preserving left-to-right index order with a fresh sprag_gui.split.dock.{seq} id. SPRAG_GUI_LAYOUT (row/grid) env retired.

view.rs view_main reads the topology and renders via pinion view_dock_surface (each leaf wrapped in view_dock_panel: a 28px header strip + the pane content). The pane content is wrapped in fill_definite so the grid fills the panel slot — the grid is no longer the direct splitter child, so without the fill its full-window intrinsic size overflowed the panel, the pane_tag rect was never measured, and the R1012 reflow never fired (caught by 3 failing tests, fixed). fill_definite moved from split.rs into view.rs beside compose; the grid-mode empty_cell hold-slot removed.

main.rs create_extra_externals walks the LIVE topology for one SplitterExternal per Split (keyed on the Split id == the painted SplitterStyle tag), and external_set_is_dynamic() -> true so a dock-back-minted split auto-registers via pinion R689 reconcile_externals (preserving surviving splitters' drag state). The boot focus_request is now guarded behind an Owner::cache factory (runs once) because the per-frame reconcile re-runs the factory and an unconditional request would re-pin focus to pane 0 every frame. dock.rs toggle_pane_floating mutates BOTH the windows signal and the split-tree at the one toggle site so they never disagree.
verification_bullets: 49 sprag-gui tests pass (the reflow test now derives expected rows from window-height-minus-28px-header; the divider-drag test targets boot_split_id(0); collapse-on-undock + index-ordered dock-back + empty-tree covered by a new split.rs guard float_collapses_and_dock_back_restores_index_order). cargo clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings --document-private-items clean. The pre-commit hook (mnemosyne validate-workspace + rustfmt --check + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets) passed on commit f987b1e.

Live GUI (cargo run -p sprag-gui on DISPLAY :0): 2 panes render with 28px headers, the divider drags, undock collapses (the other pane fills). A live [DIAG] trace surfaced a PRE-EXISTING pinion gap (NOT an R60 regression): after undock the new window's pane is not auto-focused — focus_request (one-shot mailbox) + FocusManager::update_focusable_tags clear-on-absent (focus.rs:141) race the 1-frame window creation, so the next apply_key sees focused=None. Reported as claudedocs/PINION-PR26-NEW-WINDOW-FOCUS-FOLLOW.md (no sprag workaround, per the stop-and-report-upstream-gaps ground rule); PINION-REQUIREMENTS status update 14. The flat-model removal is the user-approved migration's P1; P2 (drag-to-dock) and P3 (tear-off) not started.
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR26 (undock new-window focus-follow) reported, not delivered — sprag's route_key already requests focus on the undocked pane, so sprag consumes with 0 code change once pinion lands the sticky-focus-request / new-window-auto-focus fix.

P2 (drag-to-dock + drop preview + nested splits, via DockReorganizeExternal / resolve_dock_drop / DockDropZone) and P3 (handle-drag tear-off via DockPanelExternal) of the dock migration — not started.

dock-back loses the floated boundary's ratio (a fresh split id starts at the default 0.5) — a deliberate v1 bound; P2 drag-to-dock gives precise control. Header title is the panel_id (terminal-{i}); a friendlier title (e.g. the command label) is a later polish.

Round 61.decision_summary: Round 61: adversarial session-review remediation of R60 (two lenses — refactoring + architecture/SSOT — via subagents, plus my own source cross-check, all reconciled against the code per the R48/R59 rule). No behavior change. Both lenses confirmed R60 is the correct long-term seam with NO must-fix behavioral bug; the issues were SSOT and doc-honesty. Fixed: unified the "which panes are docked" authority onto the dock-tree (a11y had read the windows-signal while the paint read the topology — two sources for one fact), corrected three stale "single source" docs, hardened dock_pane's index-order re-insertion, and added the missing 3+-pane test. Declined the architecture lens's deeper reactive-projection rewrite as speculative P2-era wiring (YAGNI), documenting it as the P2 cleanup instead.
changes_bullets: SSOT — unified the docked-set authority onto the dock-tree. a11y::access_nodes_for_window now reads the docked set from the new split::docked_pane_indices() (the SAME source view_main paints from) instead of the windows-signal's is_pane_floating. R60 had split this fact (view read the topology, a11y read the windows-signal — two encodings of "which panes are docked" consumed by disjoint subsystems, kept consistent only by convention at the toggle site). The now-orphaned dock::is_pane_floating is removed (its window-existence check inlined in the dock test). The dock.rs module doc, which falsely claimed "Floating SSOT — the topology Signal ... read by the main-window tiling," is rewritten to "two distinct authorities: OS windows (the windows-signal) vs the docked-pane set (the dock-tree), kept consistent at the single toggle_pane_floating site."

Docs-as-SSOT — view::fill_definite's doc corrected from "compose is the SOLE caller / single enforcement point / no caller can forget it" (R59 had centralized it; R60 legitimately added a second per-leaf caller in view_main's panel_content callback) to "two enforcement points, each a different flex layer: the surface root (compose) and each leaf's content slot (because view_dock_panel interposes a sizeless flex_grow content wrapper)". The main.rs module-map heading (R32, R36, R37, R38) updated to include R60.

Robustness/honesty — split::dock_pane now sort_unstable()s the docked indices so its "first index > index" insertion point no longer silently depends on panel_ids() being pre-sorted (an emergent, unenforced invariant the rewrite relied on); the doc now states that this index-relative re-insertion is a v1 bound that P2 drag-to-dock must replace with identity-relative (drop-zone-driven) insertion once panes can be reordered (visual order != index order).
verification_bullets: Two-lens adversarial review (refactoring-expert + system-architect subagents) + my own source cross-check, every finding reconciled against the actual code (the R48/R59 lesson — verify the agents' findings AND their proposed fixes, do not just accept). Both lenses' verdict: R60 is the right long-term seam; R1.7/north-star intact (R60 touched zero sprag-host/sprag-vt files; grep-confirmed no dock-topology/ratio/layout view-state leaked into the AI-facing producer); external_set_is_dynamic + per-frame reconcile + the Owner::cache boot-focus-seed guard + the fill_definite layering are all the pinion-blessed/textbook idioms; surviving panes' split ratios are lossless across a float/dock cycle (confirmed by tracing pinion's remove_leaf_rec/split_leaf_rec cloning each surviving Split's id+ratio). The one disagreement (a11y dual-source: refactoring lens called it out-of-scope, architecture lens called it MAJOR) was resolved in favor of fixing it — the dock.rs module-doc contradiction made the smell concrete, not merely "two consistent sources".

New guard split::dock_back_inserts_in_index_order_for_3_plus_panes (4-pane: float a MIDDLE pane then dock it back = the Some(j > index) insert-before branch; float the LAST pane then dock it back = the None append-right branch — the branches the prior 2-pane-only test could not reach). 50 sprag-gui tests pass; cargo clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings --document-private-items clean; the pre-commit hook (mnemosyne validate-workspace + rustfmt --check + cargo clippy --workspace) passed on commit fc25807.
carry_forward_bullets: The architecture lens's deeper recommendation — make the docked set a reactive PROJECTION of one authority (an Effect subscribed to the windows-signal that reconciles the tree's leaf-set) rather than co-mutating both signals at the toggle site — is deferred to P2. No second mutation path exists yet (P2 drag-to-dock is the first), so it would be speculative wiring tested against nothing (YAGNI); it is documented in dock.rs as the P2-era cleanup the toggle-site invariant points to.
PINION-PR26 (undock new-window focus-follow) still filed, not delivered — sprag consumes with 0 change once pinion lands it.

P2 (drag-to-dock + drop preview + nested splits) and P3 (handle-drag tear-off) of the dock migration — not started. The dock_pane index-relative re-insertion must move to identity-relative (drop-zone-driven) when P2 lands.
