publishable_changes_bullets: SSOT — unified the docked-set authority onto the dock-tree. a11y::access_nodes_for_window now reads the docked set from the new split::docked_pane_indices() (the SAME source view_main paints from) instead of the windows-signal's is_pane_floating. R60 had split this fact (view read the topology, a11y read the windows-signal — two encodings of "which panes are docked" consumed by disjoint subsystems, kept consistent only by convention at the toggle site). The now-orphaned dock::is_pane_floating is removed (its window-existence check inlined in the dock test). The dock.rs module doc, which falsely claimed "Floating SSOT — the topology Signal ... read by the main-window tiling," is rewritten to "two distinct authorities: OS windows (the windows-signal) vs the docked-pane set (the dock-tree), kept consistent at the single toggle_pane_floating site."

Docs-as-SSOT — view::fill_definite's doc corrected from "compose is the SOLE caller / single enforcement point / no caller can forget it" (R59 had centralized it; R60 legitimately added a second per-leaf caller in view_main's panel_content callback) to "two enforcement points, each a different flex layer: the surface root (compose) and each leaf's content slot (because view_dock_panel interposes a sizeless flex_grow content wrapper)". The main.rs module-map heading (R32, R36, R37, R38) updated to include R60.

Robustness/honesty — split::dock_pane now sort_unstable()s the docked indices so its "first index > index" insertion point no longer silently depends on panel_ids() being pre-sorted (an emergent, unenforced invariant the rewrite relied on); the doc now states that this index-relative re-insertion is a v1 bound that P2 drag-to-dock must replace with identity-relative (drop-zone-driven) insertion once panes can be reordered (visual order != index order).
publishable_verification_bullets: Two-lens adversarial review (refactoring-expert + system-architect subagents) + my own source cross-check, every finding reconciled against the actual code (the R48/R59 lesson — verify the agents' findings AND their proposed fixes, do not just accept). Both lenses' verdict: R60 is the right long-term seam; R1.7/north-star intact (R60 touched zero sprag-host/sprag-vt files; grep-confirmed no dock-topology/ratio/layout view-state leaked into the AI-facing producer); external_set_is_dynamic + per-frame reconcile + the Owner::cache boot-focus-seed guard + the fill_definite layering are all the pinion-blessed/textbook idioms; surviving panes' split ratios are lossless across a float/dock cycle (confirmed by tracing pinion's remove_leaf_rec/split_leaf_rec cloning each surviving Split's id+ratio). The one disagreement (a11y dual-source: refactoring lens called it out-of-scope, architecture lens called it MAJOR) was resolved in favor of fixing it — the dock.rs module-doc contradiction made the smell concrete, not merely "two consistent sources".

New guard split::dock_back_inserts_in_index_order_for_3_plus_panes (4-pane: float a MIDDLE pane then dock it back = the Some(j > index) insert-before branch; float the LAST pane then dock it back = the None append-right branch — the branches the prior 2-pane-only test could not reach). 50 sprag-gui tests pass; cargo clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings --document-private-items clean; the pre-commit hook (mnemosyne validate-workspace + rustfmt --check + cargo clippy --workspace) passed on commit fc25807.

Round 64.decision_summary: Round 64: reproduced the dock double-toggle bug HEADLESSLY (the live "Ctrl+Shift+Enter docks-then-undocks from the 2nd action" that R63's PR-27 consumption did NOT fix). Pinion R1071's OS-focus gate is defeated by close-during-dispatch: one physical press is double-delivered, the FIRST dispatch docks the floated pane and CLOSES its window, OS focus moves to main, so the SECOND delivery (to main, now focused) passes the gate and undocks = bounce. Filed the follow-up requirement R27.4 in the PINION-PR27 doc + REQUIREMENTS 16. Added an ignored reproduction guard that FAILS on R1071 and flips green when R27.4 lands. KEY methodological lesson: my R63 e2e guard passed FALSELY because it hand-pinned note_os_focus instead of modeling the focus moving as a SIDE EFFECT of the dock closing the window — a synthetic test where I script both the inputs AND the intermediate state only verifies the model I already believe, not an emergent interaction I did not model.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui/src/main.rs: new ignored test multiwindow_dock_does_not_bounce_when_close_moves_focus. It drives the live sequence through the real ShellCore via pinion R1071's key_press_for_window + note_os_focus seam (R27.2): note_os_focus(pane-0, true) -> key_press_for_window(pane-0) docks pane 0 and closes its window -> note_os_focus(pane-0, false) + note_os_focus(main, true) [THE step the prior guard omitted: closing the focused window moves OS focus to main] -> key_press_for_window(main) passes the gate -> undock -> windows.len() == 2 (bounce). It asserts the FIXED behaviour (== 1), so it FAILS on R1071 = reproduces the live bug; un-ignore it when the pinion R27.4 fix lands. The DIAG eprintln added to apply_key_repeat for the live REPEAT+timestamp capture was removed (net-zero vs R63's committed code).

Running the guard with --ignored FAILS with left:2 right:1 (the bounce) = reproduces the live bug; the sibling multiwindow_dock_chord_toggles_once_per_press still PASSES (it covers the focus-STAYS re-delivery R1071 DOES gate, a real partial guarantee). The bug + diagnosis were confirmed from a live apply_key_repeat REPEAT+timestamp DIAG trace: one physical press in the 2-window state = dispatch #1 dock + dispatch #2 undock (32ms apart, REPEAT=false, both focused=pane.1), and window-create=1-event vs window-close=2-events isolates the window-close as the trigger.

Round 65.decision_summary: Round 65: consumed pinion R1073 (the press-owner snapshot) and closed PINION-PR27 R27.4 -- the live "Ctrl+Shift+Enter docks-then-undocks from the 2nd action" dock/undock bounce is FIXED. R1073 pins the OS-focus decision of a physical press to its FIRST-admit owner window, so the close-during-dispatch path (1st dispatch docks the floated pane, closes its window, OS focus moves to main, 2nd delivery of the SAME press reaches the now-focused main) is gated -- the re-delivery is dropped because the press did not begin on main. sprag bumped the 7 pinion-* revs 21ca4953 -> d9b9a5a4 and un-ignored the reproduction guard (now green). Methodological close on R64: the two multiwindow guards were restructured to float pane 0 via toggle_pane_floating DIRECTLY rather than via a 1st key press, because a key-driven 1st undock pins the press owner to main and that is what defeated the press under test -- the test setup, not the fix, was masking the green.

Round 67.decision_summary: Round 67: bumped pinion d9b9a5a4 -> e2cb06f2 (R1078.1) to consume PINION-PR28, fixing the live dock-flap (one held Ctrl+Shift+Enter flapped the pane dock/undock up to 24 times). Root cause (corrected from a wrong first hypothesis): the dock toggle moves OS focus, winit emits synthetic focus-transition key events AND resets its own repeat detector on the focus change, so real auto-repeat presses after the bounce came through as is_synthetic=false repeat=false and re-fired the toggle. Fixed in pinion in two steps (R1076 exclude synthetic from dispatch; R1078 derive the repeat flag from the press-owner, not winit's event.repeat). sprag code unchanged; verified via the R66 SPRAG_GUI_LOG trace: a 2-3s hold now logs exactly one toggle (was four).
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml: bumped the 7 pinion-* revs d9b9a5a4 (R65) -> e2cb06f2 (pinion R1078.1); SCE 3078f8bf / vello 0.9 unchanged; Cargo.lock regenerated. Consumes PINION-PR28 (the live dock-flap: one held Ctrl+Shift+Enter flapped the focused pane dock/undock 24 times). The fix landed in two pinion steps: R1076 made KeyboardInput consult winit's is_synthetic and exclude synthetic focus-transition key events from dispatch + the press-owner lifecycle (necessary -- removed the synthetic-press re-trigger -- but INSUFFICIENT on its own); R1078/R1078.1 then derived the dispatch repeat flag from pinion's own press-owner state instead of winit's event.repeat, because winit resets its repeat detector on every focus change, so a real auto-repeat press arriving after the toggle's own focus bounce was mis-flagged repeat=false and slipped past the toggle-class repeat-drop.
No sprag code change: sprag's focus-follow + dock toggle were correct; the bug was entirely in how the held-key dispatch was gated upstream.
verification_bullets: cargo build -p sprag-gui clean on R1078.1; 54 sprag-gui tests + full cargo test --workspace green; clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings clean. Live verified through the R66 SPRAG_GUI_LOG trace on a real winit X11 hold: BEFORE (R1076) a 2-3s hold logged 4 dock toggles (still flapping); AFTER (R1078.1) the same hold logs exactly ONE toggle (undock pane 1: windows 1 -> 2) and nothing further -- the auto-repeat presses are now gated upstream and never reach sprag. The flap is gone.
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR28 (focus-change synthetic key events + focus-reset repeat flag flapping the dock chord) DELIVERED (pinion R1076 is_synthetic gate + R1078 repeat-from-press-owner) and CONSUMED (sprag R67). No open pinion blockers. The PINION-PR28 doc + REQUIREMENTS 18 record the full root cause incl. the corrected diagnosis (the first hypothesis -- X11 non-detectable autorepeat -- was wrong; winit enables detectable autorepeat, the real cause was synthetic focus events + the focus-reset repeat flag).

Bumped the 7 pinion-* revs e2cb06f2 (R1078.1) -> 7bd8a1d2 (R1087.1) across PINION-PR29 (R1080-82: DockPanelExternal R742 drag hooks + DockReorganizer + DockDropPreview), PR-29.1 (R1084: DockReorganizer total over Option<DockTopology>, so sprag's collapse-to-None topology drives the coordinator directly with no second signal), and PR-30 (R1086: LayoutStyle.min_size + view_splitter flex-child main-axis min:0, so a vertical split's panels shrink to their ratio instead of overflowing). Tier 3 live tear-off (the window follows the cursor during the drag), chosen by the user, is still owed pinion R1088 -- R1087 added only the WindowSpec position foundation.

carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR29 / PR-29.1 / PR-30 DELIVERED + CONSUMED. Drag-to-dock splits (horizontal + vertical) + tabs (center) work live. split::dock_pane kept index-relative on purpose: drag positioning is reorganizer-driven (SplitInsert/Swap) and bypasses dock_pane; the key re-dock has no drop position, so index-relative is the right default (the old P2 MUST-DO is resolved/reframed, not skipped).

PINION-PR31 (Tier 3 live tear-off, user-chosen: the floating window follows the cursor during the drag) is PARTIALLY delivered: pinion R1087 added the WindowSpec.position SSOT + move-on-change foundation, but the drag-follow runtime loop is owed pinion R1088 (NOT yet delivered; origin/main is R1087.1). Until R1088, tear-off stays release-driven (works via the bug-A fix). sprag consumption (early-detach / follow / redock wiring) waits on R1088. PR-31 likely subsumes P4 (cross-window drag-back = same window-follows-cursor + dock-detect machine).

Lesson re-burned (R67 family): headless-green missed two live bugs -- the tear-off guard built the bare tear_off tag and passed while the live wire delivers the scoped {panel}.tear_off, and no vertical-split render guard existed so the min:auto overflow shipped as done. Faithful guards must match the live wire AND assert the actual rendered layout, not just the data path.

Round 69.decision_summary: Round 69: consumed PINION-PR31 (Tier 3 live cursor-following tear-off) in sprag-gui. Bumped the 7 pinion-* revs 7bd8a1d2 (R1087.1) -> 9d13cb8c (R1095): pinion delivered the live tear-off across R1088 (scene/window_move + WindowEvent::Moved feedback + echo-latch = the WindowSpec.position foundation), R1093 (the router forwards the absolute drag cursor to the source via drag_to_at/drag_release_at, even on a tag escape), and R1094 (live cursor-following tear-off = the non-toggling tear_off_follow / tear_off_redock seam the DockPanelExternal emits, in pinion-widget-paint). SCE 3078f8bf / vello 0.9 unchanged. Wired the seam onto sprag's two-authority dock model: non-toggling dock::float_pane_at (ensure floating + track the desktop-converted cursor as the window's outer position) and dock::redock_pane (ensure docked, idempotent), with toggle_pane_floating now delegating to both so the key path, the drag tear-off and the redock share two window/topology co-mutation sites. Round 7.decision_summary: Headless multiplexing: a pane registry + lifecycle (spawn/close/resize) + per-pane I/O addressing exposed through a workspace-control External; geometric tiling deferred to the GUI round as a rendering concern.
changes_bullets: New module crates/sprag-terminal/src/workspace.rs: pinion-free pane registry (Workspace) -- PaneId, Pane, spawn/close/resize/list over TerminalSession (producer-layer concern, R5 layering).

New crates/sprag-host/src/workspace.rs: WorkspaceExternal control surface holding Arc<Mutex<Workspace>>; scene/invoke actions spawn/close/resize and scene/query panes -- generalizes the R6 External+invoke carrier (no new RPC methods).

Scene is now a workspace Container[ pane_<id>[TextGrid + input External] ... + sprag_mux control External ]: lib.rs workspace_scene() assembles it (releasing the workspace lock before dispatch so invoke can re-lock); rpc.rs serve/handle_request take Arc<Mutex<Workspace>>; bin starts a one-pane workspace.

Input addresses a pane explicitly (/pane_<id>/sprag_input/external/key) -- no focus state; per-pane sizing is producer-set (no layout pass). Geometric tiling (split tree/ratios) intentionally absent: it only has meaning relative to a display surface, so it is deferred to the GUI round.
verification_bullets: 52 workspace tests pass (sprag-vt 12, sprag-input 11, sprag-grid 4, sprag-terminal 5, sprag-host 20); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

Bin end-to-end (sprag-term -- cat): scene/invoke /sprag_mux/external/spawn -> pane id 1; scene/query /sprag_mux/external/panes lists both panes with dims+labels; scene/snapshot root is Container[sprag_workspace] with children pane_0, pane_1, sprag_mux; per-pane scene/invoke key echoes onto the addressed pane's grid.

Stop-and-report check: pinion needs nothing new -- nested Container resolve/snapshot is rect-independent and needs no layout/Owner (pinion's own invoke.rs/resolve.rs tests), windows are SCXML statechart states (not scene primitives), and the dock split substrate (pinion-widget-paint::dock) is GUI-chrome-oriented (its home is the future GUI round).
carry_forward_bullets: Geometric tiling (split tree, ratios, screen-division -> cols/rows) deferred to the GUI render round; its home is pinion's pinion-widget-paint::dock (DockNode/DockTopology), GPU-free but GUI-chrome/drag oriented.
Organizational grouping (sessions/tabs) and a directional focus pointer are deferred -- human/GUI conveniences; headless uses explicit per-pane addressing.
Pane auto-removal on child exit is not modeled (a pane persists after its child exits, showing its final screen); revisit when a lifecycle policy is wanted.
Next headless-control-stack step (rendering-waits roadmap): orchestration -- AI<->AI loops with termination/depth/cost guardrails, to be modeled as SCXML statecharts codegen'd via SCE.

Round 70.decision_summary: Round 70: fixed the R69 live tear-off follow gap, and corrected an R69 overclaim. R69's "follow live-verified" was wrong: the RPC scene/drag verification batch-injects every cursor move before any reconcile, which masked that the float reconcile dropped the source pane's DockPanelExternal (R69 registered the externals for the DOCKED panes only). In a real mouse drag, events arrive one at a time with reconciles between them, so the first escaped move floated the pane, external_set_is_dynamic re-ran create_extra_externals mid-drag and removed the in-progress drag's external, and the follow died after one frame (redock never reached). Fix: register a DockPanelExternal for ALL panes, not just the docked ones -- the symmetric model pinion's reference consumer uses (hello-dock-panels: one DockPanelExternal per panel, docked and floating sharing it). The source external now survives the float reconcile (R689 preserve-by-tag keeps its drag state), so the captured main-window gesture continues: escape -> follow, return-over-zone -> redock. Live-confirmed on a real winit X11 instance: one header drag produced 915 continuous tear_off_follow emits (R69 stopped at 1), and redock fired via both the continuous-gesture return (tear_off_redock) and Ctrl+Shift+Enter.
changes_bullets: main.rs create_extra_externals: register the R742 DockPanelExternal for ALL panes (0..pane_count) at panel_id(i), not just split::docked_pane_indices(). A tear-off is one continuous press captured by the source pane's external; the first escaped move floats that pane, a topology change that re-runs this factory (external_set_is_dynamic) MID-DRAG. Docked-only registration dropped the in-progress drag's external on that reconcile (follow stopped after one frame, redock unreachable). All-pane registration keeps it (R689 preserve-by-tag preserves the drag state). Matches pinion hello-dock-panels' symmetric one-DockPanelExternal-per-panel model (docked + floating share it).

Added the regression guard dock_panel_external_survives_the_float_reconcile: create_extra_externals lists a panel_id external for every pane while docked, and STILL lists the floated pane's external after toggle_pane_floating (the float reconcile). The continuous gesture-with-reconcile can't be synthesized headlessly (an RPC batch delivers every move before any reconcile -- exactly what masked this in R69), so the guard pins the registration invariant directly.
verification_bullets: sprag-gui 60/0 (was 59; +1 guard) + full cargo test --workspace green; clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings (private items) clean.

Live-confirmed on a real winit X11 instance via SPRAG_GUI_LOG + scene/windows: a single header drag produced 915 continuous tear_off_follow emits (R69 produced 1 then stalled); redock observed via the continuous-gesture return (tear_off_redock, 4x) and via Ctrl+Shift+Enter. The "follow live-verified" claim in the R69 changelog is corrected here: R69's RPC scene/drag batch-injects all moves before any reconcile, so it could not surface the reconcile-removes-external bug -- an RPC batch is not live event-by-event-with-reconcile (the R67/R68 lesson, sharper).
carry_forward_bullets: Re-grabbing a SETTLED floating window (reposition / re-tear) needs a header painted on the floating window: view::view_for_window's floating branch currently paints the bare pane (no view_dock_panel header) -- sprag Fix B, the next round. The all-pane DockPanelExternal is already registered, so the header just needs to paint at panel_id(i).

Dragging a settled floating window BACK onto the main dock to redock is the per-window-router-bound cross-window gap (resolve_drop_point hit-tests only the dragging window's own scene) -- filed as PINION-PR33. Redock today works via the continuous-gesture return or Ctrl+Shift+Enter.

Escape-based vs threshold detach: pinion R1094 detaches only on escape (over==None); the user wants browser-tab "float on grab" (threshold detach) -- filed as PINION-PR32 (revisits PR-31 doc's original threshold proposal; coexists with reorganize via the source-window capture). Both PR-32/PR-33 await the pinion author.

Round 71.decision_summary: Round 71: adversarial session-review remediation of R69/R70 (the PR-31 live-tear-off follow consumption + the symmetric-external fix), following the R52/R59/R61 pattern -- two independent review lenses (refactoring + architecture/SSOT) plus a self source cross-check, reconciled against the code. Verdict: the seam is substantially textbook. The north-star isolation is COMPILE-ENFORCED (sprag-host, the AI/headless crate that owns SpragPaneExternal + the RPC scene/* projection, has no dependency on pinion-shell/widget-paint/runtime, so window/dock types are unreachable there -- a structural guarantee, not discipline). The SSOT invariant "a pane floats iff its window exists AND its leaf is absent" provably holds across all entry points, and the reactive-projection cleanup R61 deferred is a correct YAGNI (only docked membership is derivable; the split-tree also holds shape/ratios no projection reconstructs). Applied the should-fix findings: split the three-behavior ensure_pane_floating into push_float (the one float co-mutation) + open_floating (key path) + a single-borrow float_pane_at; rewrote the reducer to split the scoped tag once and route by the trusted tag prefix (killing per-follow-move format! allocations); renamed + strengthened the R70 guard to a set equality; and documented a verified v1 placement bound (redock-over-zone lands index-relative because pinion's apply_intent runs synchronously before the enqueued redock and SplitInsert rejects on the absent source) filed as PINION-PR34. No behavior change.
changes_bullets: dock.rs (F8 SRP + F1 single-borrow): replaced ensure_pane_floating -- which did create OR reposition OR a None no-op, each caller using a disjoint subset -- with push_float (the single window+tree float co-mutation, shared), open_floating (the cursor-less key-path float), and a rewritten float_pane_at that does create-or-reposition over ONE topology borrow (the main-window origin and the repositioned window come from the same snapshot, so a concurrent WindowEvent::Moved write-back can't make the position stale). The None no-op overload is gone; toggle_pane_floating calls open_floating(None). undock_window_spec position via if-let; module + redock_pane docs updated (the float/dock asymmetry; the projection cleanup is only partially derivable).

main.rs (F2/F3): the reducer splits the scoped {panel}.{event} tag ONCE via rsplit_once and routes by the trusted tag prefix, matching (event, payload). Removes the per-arm format!("{panel}.{EVENT}") String allocation that fired on every follow intent (per drag-move, hundreds per gesture), and stops routing by the payload's panel field (the tag is the SSOT routing key, the payload is data).

main.rs (F9 + doc nits): renamed the R70 guard dock_panel_external_survives_the_float_reconcile -> dock_panel_external_registered_for_every_pane_across_a_float (no longer over-promising gesture-survival the headless test can't reach -- R689 drag-state preservation is pinion's) and strengthened it from two contains() to a SET equality (catches a regression dropping ANY pane). Added the why-dormant-is-safe note (registration is a superset of painted tags; dispatch hit-tests painted scenes) + the redock-over-zone v1-bound note with the PINION-PR34 pointer.
verification_bullets: No behavior change: the R69 live-wire guards (tear_off_follow float-then-reposition, tear_off_redock dock-then-noop) pass unchanged on the refactored float_pane_at + reducer; sprag-gui 60/0; full cargo test --workspace green; clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings (private items) clean.

Review method (R52/R59/R61 pattern): two async adversarial lenses (refactoring-expert + system-architect) over the committed R69 (b681143) + R70 (10a01fa) diffs, plus a self source cross-check that VERIFIED the architecture lens's redock finding against pinion's SplitInsert::apply (topology.remove_leaf(source)? rejects on the absent source) -- correcting sprag's own first-pass hypothesis (reorganizer-places-then-dock_pane-noops) which was wrong. The lenses also corrected each other: the architecture lens's pinion-source read confirmed the refactoring lens's flagged "dormant external" as safe-by-construction (registration is a model-scene superset; dispatch routes only painted tags).
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR34 filed: redock-over-zone lands index-relative (drop-zone fidelity lost) because pinion's drag_release runs reorganizer.apply_intent synchronously before the enqueued tear_off_redock drains, and SplitInsert's remove_leaf(source)? rejects on the detached source's absent leaf. Round 73.decision_summary: Round 73 (Stage A of the approved collapse-to-placeholder migration): flip sprag's dock model so a floated pane's leaf STAYS in the split-tree instead of being removed. This is the structural prerequisite for zone-honoring cross-window redock (the leaf must exist for the reorganizer's apply_zone_redock to relocate it) and it simultaneously lands R61's deferred SSOT cleanup. The windows-signal becomes the SOLE floating authority (a pane floats IFF its pane-{i} WindowSpec exists); the DockTopology becomes the SOLE shape/ratio authority, holding every pane's leaf always and never co-mutated by float/dock. The docked set (read by paint + a11y) is now DERIVED -- the tree's leaves filtered by is_pane_floating -- so it can never disagree with the windows-signal. A floating leaf paints a placeholder (pinion's view_floating_placeholder) holding its slot; its real content lives in its own undock window. The tree is restructured only by a reorganize gesture, never by a plain float/dock. Mirrors pinion's hello-dock-panels-editor reference consumer. No new user capability yet (the drag-back redock seam is Stage C); this is the model flip plus the placeholder paint.

Rewrote docked_pane_indices to filter the full leaf set by !crate::dock::is_pane_floating(i) (the derived membership). use_dock_topology stays Option (None = zero-pane edge) and is always Some after boot. Rewrote the module + fn docs to the placeholder/orthogonal-authorities invariant. Trimmed DockSplitPosition/TopologyError/SplitterOrientation imports.

Round 77.decision_summary: Round 77: make the dock model SELECTABLE (collapse | placeholder) and change the DEFAULT back to collapse. R72-R75 made placeholder the model (a torn-off pane HOLDS its slot); live-testing it the user found the held slot un-terminal-multiplexer-like -- they expect the remaining terminals to FILL the screen when one tears off (tmux/zellij = the original R60 collapse model). So: a new DockMode enum + dock_mode() selector reads SPRAG_GUI_DOCK_MODE (collapse default | placeholder opt-in); the R73-deleted collapse primitives split::float_pane/dock_pane are restored and called by dock::push_float/redock_pane ONLY in collapse mode. The change is contained -- the two models differ in exactly one fact (does float/dock mutate the split-tree); view/main-reducer/a11y are unchanged because both modes flow through the same downstream code (in collapse a floated pane has no leaf so the placeholder branch is never reached; in placeholder the leaf is filtered). Honest trade preserved in the docs: collapse default = siblings reclaim space, BUT cross-window zone-honoring redock (R75) degrades to index-relative (the leaf is gone, can't be zone-placed); placeholder opt-in = zone-honoring redock but the slot is held.
changes_bullets: dock.rs: added enum DockMode { Collapse, Placeholder } + DockMode::from_env (SPRAG_GUI_DOCK_MODE, placeholder->Placeholder else Collapse) + dock_mode() backed by an Owner::cache'd Cell<DockMode> (per-owner so tests select either mode; a Cell not a Signal -- the mode is a boot constant, not a reactive paint input) + a #[cfg(test)] set_dock_mode seam. push_float and redock_pane now gate the tree mutation: `if dock_mode()==Collapse { split::float_pane(i) }` / `{ split::dock_pane(i) }`. Module doc rewritten: the windows-signal/tree relationship is mode-dependent (collapse co-mutates, placeholder orthogonal).

split.rs: RESTORED float_pane (remove_leaf/RootRemoval->None) + dock_pane (index-relative re-insert) + next_dock_split_id/SPLIT_SEQ_KEY + the imports (TopologyError, DockSplitPosition, SplitterOrientation) -- called by dock only in collapse mode. Module doc rewritten to "two selectable models" + a "why both exist (R60->R72->R77)" section keeping each model's rationale.

main.rs/split.rs tests: mode-gated. undock_all_panes_paints_placeholders + tear_off_redock_at_relocates + docked_membership_filters set Placeholder mode; tear_off_intent_floats now asserts the DEFAULT collapse (the leaf is removed, len 1, not 2). Added collapse_float_removes_the_leaf_and_dock_restores_index_order (split.rs) exercising the restored R60 primitives directly.

OPT-IN (SPRAG_GUI_DOCK_MODE=placeholder): floating pane 1 keeps terminal-1's leaf in the tree and paints terminal-1_placeholder holding the slot, content in its own window. Both confirmed end to end.

Round 79.decision_summary: Round 79: fix the "settled floating window won't drag" path by threading source_window. pinion R1107 added a source_window field to the tear_off_follow payload (which window the cursor was measured in), but R78 bumped past it without consuming it -- so float_pane_at hardcoded the main window's origin in its own cursor_to_desktop. For a SETTLED floating window dragged by its own header the cursor is in that window's frame, so main-origin + a local cursor = a bogus desktop point and the window jumped/froze. Fix: float_pane_at now takes source_window: Option<&str> and uses pinion's pinion_shell::desktop_position_from (the SSOT pinion R1107.1 lifted to the shell) instead of the hand-rolled cursor_to_desktop (deleted); the reducer reads source_window from the follow Json and threads it. None falls back to main, as before. NOTE: live floater re-drag itself is still a pinion parked HW path (r1107), so this has no behavior change until pinion delivers that -- it pre-positions the correct consumption so the floater re-drag lands right when it arrives. This was MY omission (a new payload field on the R78 bump went unconsumed), not a HW-gated case -- the added headless guard proves it was catchable.
changes_bullets: dock.rs: float_pane_at(i, source_window, cursor) -- deleted the local cursor_to_desktop (hardcoded MAIN origin) and now calls pinion_shell::desktop_position_from(&windows, source_window, cursor), the pub SSOT pinion R1107.1 lifted to the shell so the consumer needn't re-derive the origin. source_window=None -> main; Some("pane-{i}") -> that floater's origin. Doc rewritten to name the settled-floater bug.

main.rs reducer follow arm: read source_window from the Json (v.get("source_window")) and pass it to float_pane_at. Added guard dragging_a_settled_floating_window_uses_its_own_origin: give main a known origin (1000,500), float pane 1 with source_window=main (-> 1300,700), then a source_window=pane-1 follow with a local cursor (10,5) lands at (1310,705) -- ITS OWN origin, not main's (the bug would give 1010,505). Driven through the real reducer with the exact scoped tag + source_window Json the live wire carries.

Source-confirmed the fragments conflict: PR-32 instant-detach gives "follows on grab" but breaks in-dock split; PR-36 escape-detach gives split but kills the immediacy; floater re-drag (2) is parked; OS-titlebar drag (2') only records position (note_window_moved), no dock. PR-38 proposes (A) split the drag-GHOST from detach (grab -> ghost follows, drop-time decides zone->split / outside->float; mode-agnostic) + unify the grab surface on the app header (decorations-off, VS Code way).

Round 8.decision_summary: Orchestration control substrate: a guardrailed perceive-act-judge loop over a pane, modeled as an SCE/SCXML statechart (sprag's first direct SCE dogfood); built in-process, with the plugin host/API to be extracted later.
changes_bullets: New crate crates/sprag-orchestrator: orchestration.scxml (datamodel=null pure-control perceive->act->judge loop) codegen'd in build.rs via sce_build::compile_scxml, driven by an Orchestrator over a pane's SessionHandle (R7) using the R6 sprag-input encoder. Pinion-free.

Guardrails: iteration budget + cost budget (injected-bytes proxy) + sentinel convergence, surfaced as three <final> states (Converged/Exhausted/Failed). Counters live in the Rust loop; the statechart owns the control topology + termination branching (pinion's datamodel=null widget pattern).

SCE dependency wired to pinion's vendored vendor/sce (kept synced to canonical scxml-core-engine), NOT the canonical path directly: pinion already path-deps vendor/sce, so a second same-version path source collides in the Cargo lockfile. Sharing pinion's path yields one SCE package, content-identical to canonical.

Framing: orchestration built as a concrete in-process capability first; the plugin host / extension API is extracted later once a 2nd consumer reveals the contract (abstraction-needs-second-consumer). Real AI<->AI (adapters), multi-pane relay, and RPC exposure deferred.
verification_bullets: 55 workspace tests pass (+3 orchestrator: exhaust-after-N-iterations, converge-on-sentinel, cost-budget-terminates); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean (generated state machine is allow-wrapped).

SCE codegen runs in sprag-orchestrator/build.rs (orchestration_sm.rs in OUT_DIR, inner-attrs stripped per pinion's pattern); runtime drives Engine<OrchestrationPolicy> via initialize/process_event/get_current_state/is_in_final_state. Confirmed pinion's vendored SCE sce-build+sce-rust-runtime are content-identical to canonical before depending on them.

Stop-and-report exercised: a Cargo lockfile package collision (canonical vs pinion-vendored sce-build v0.1.0, same version, different paths) halted the build and was reported, not worked around; resolved after the user synced pinion's vendored SCE to canonical, by depending on pinion's vendored path (one SCE package == canonical).
carry_forward_bullets: RPC OrchestratorExternal: start/configure an orchestration via scene/invoke and observe it via scene/query (mirror WorkspaceExternal), so an external AI peer drives orchestration as scene-as-data.
Multi-pane relay (A<->B): route a source pane's output as a destination pane's input -- two cross-wired drive loops; the substrate primitive generalizes to it.

AI-tool adapters (claude/aider in panes with structured I/O) are the real AI<->AI consumers; cost guardrail becomes real token/$ accounting (currently an injected-bytes proxy; SCE has no f64, so integer-only).
A depth/recursion guardrail for nested orchestration (statechart edit).
Plugin-host / extension-API extraction once orchestration + a 2nd consumer exist.
SCE dep tracks pinion's vendored copy; if pinion un-vendors or the copies diverge again, revisit (stop-and-report).

Round 83.decision_summary: Round 83: bump the 7 pinion-* git revs 6f0c1281 (R1118) -> a6e33b68 (R1120), consuming PINION-PR39 (the floater title-bar move jitter fix sprag filed R82). R1119 added a jitter harness; R1120 = desktop-frame window-move: the shell now stamps DragUpdate.source_window_origin (the floater's actual outer position) on every move, and DockPanelExternal computes the WINDOW_MOVE delta as a DESKTOP-frame increment instead of cursor - press_cursor in the moving window's own local frame. Round 84.decision_summary: Round 84: bump the 7 pinion-* git revs a6e33b68 (R1120) -> e4b76342 (R1123) and consume the new client-side window-chrome hook (R1121-R1123) to give the borderless floating pane windows their own min/max buttons + resize border -- the chrome R82 noted was missing when it made the floaters borderless (with_decorations(false)). NOTE up front: this bump does NOT fix the user's "끌어서 dock 안돼" (drag a settled floating window onto main to redock) -- that floater->main cross-window redock is still owed by pinion (PR-38 #2-redock / PR-33 live tail). R1121-R1123 are window chrome only. The new WidgetView::window_chrome hook defaults to None (naked borderless), so without consuming it sprag's floaters would stay button-less; R84 implements it (the R79/R82 bump discipline: audit + wire the new seam, not just bump). sprag returns chrome for a pane-{i} floating window (min + max + resize) and None for main (which keeps OS decorations). The floating chrome OMITS close: pinion's ChromeAction::Close routes to event_loop.exit() (whole-app quit; per-window close is an un-delivered pinion follow-up) and a floater IS a live pane, so an X must not kill the terminal -- dock the pane back (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) to close the window. SCE 3078f8bf / vello 0.9 unchanged.
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml: bumped 7 pinion-* a6e33b68 -> e4b76342 (SCE/vello untouched, 7+0 verified). main.rs: implemented WidgetView::window_chrome(window_id) -> for a pane-{i} floating window, Some(WindowChromeStyle::default() with show_close=false) (min/max glyphs + 8 resize-border regions, routed to winit actions by the shell); for main (and any non-pane id), None (keeps OS decorations). Imported WindowChromeStyle from pinion_shell (re-exported there so no pinion-overlay dep needed). WindowChromeStyle is #[non_exhaustive] so the close flag is cleared on a default()-derived value, not a struct literal.

Round 86.decision_summary: Round 86: bump the 7 pinion-* git revs e4b76342 (R1123) -> c8550c11 (R1173) -- a large pinion dock rework (~50 commits, R1124-R1173) that finally delivers the user's blocked "끌어서 dock" (drag a SETTLED floating window onto main to REDOCK) plus a proper window-close seam. Exactly ONE compile break: DockReorganizer::apply_zone_redock was retired (R1128) and the redock SSOT rebuilt around resolve_drop. An Explore agent mapped the full change-list against pinion's hello-dock-panels-editor reference; sprag mirrors it. Two consumption changes wired: (1) the TEAR_OFF_REDOCK_AT_EVENT reducer arm now classifies the drop with resolve_drop -> DropResolution and applies the outcome (Dock/OuterDock relocate + de-float, SnapBack de-float, Float stays floating), replacing the unconditional apply_zone_redock + redock_pane; the placeholder strip is dropped (resolve_drop folds it). (2) implemented WidgetView::window_close_requested (pinion R1170 seam): a floater's close docks the pane back + returns true (no app-exit), so floaters now SHOW close (R84/R85 had to omit it because close==app-quit); main returns false (close = app-quit, the right primary-close). The cross-window redock that was owed since R83 (PR-38 ②-redock / PR-33) is delivered by pinion's R1148->R1163b (the shell composes over_window across windows); sprag's arm + existing with_floating_window wiring consume it. SCE/vello unchanged.
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml: bumped 7 pinion-* e4b76342 -> c8550c11 (SCE/vello untouched, 7+0). main.rs reducer TEAR_OFF_REDOCK_AT_EVENT arm: resolve_drop(Some(&DropPoint{tag:target,x_rel,y_rel}), &panel_id(i), |t| reorganizer.is_panel(t), reorganizer.tabbing()) -> match DropResolution { Dock{target,zone}=>dock_panel_at_resolved_zone+redock_pane, OuterDock{edge}=>dock_panel_outer+redock_pane, SnapBack=>redock_pane, Float=>stay floating }. Imports: DropPoint (pinion_core::external), resolve_drop+DropResolution (pinion_widget_paint::dock).

Round 87.decision_summary: Round 87: two dock-UX fixes surfaced by live-testing R86's "끌어서 dock", both sprag-side. (1) The user found that once ALL panes are floated the main dock is EMPTY and a floater can no longer be dragged back — an empty dock has no interior drop target (pinion synthesizes an outer-dock band from the window rect, but only at the 32px rim; the interior is dead, and the editor "seeds Some and never empties" so pinion never hit this). The user chose tmux/zellij semantics: the main window always keeps at least one docked pane. So in COLLAPSE mode a float that would empty the dock (the last docked pane) is REFUSED (float_would_empty_the_dock gate at open_floating + float_pane_at's create branch); PLACEHOLDER mode keeps the leaf so it's unaffected. (2) The user noticed pinion's editor shows a drop-preview while dragging but sprag did not — sprag had left WidgetView::dock_drop_preview at its None default and had no same-window outer-preview overlay. Implemented dock_drop_preview (classify through the SAME resolve_drop SSOT the redock arm applies, so preview == result: Dock -> dock_drop_preview_overlay, OuterDock -> dock_outer_preview_overlay, Float/SnapBack -> None) + the view_main OUTER_DOCK_ZONE_TAG overlay (dock_outer_zone_highlight). Both mirror the editor. Also added a standing redock_resolution diag (the diag.rs typed-event idiom) to read a "drag that does nothing" off the log. No pin bump (consumes the already-pinned c8550c11).
changes_bullets: dock.rs: float_would_empty_the_dock(i) — collapse + pane i is the ONLY docked pane (docked_pane_indices()==[i]); gated at open_floating (early return) + float_pane_at's create branch (early return). Doc: tmux semantics, why an empty dock has no interior drop target. Guard collapse_refuses_to_float_the_last_docked_pane_placeholder_allows_it.

main.rs: WidgetView::dock_drop_preview(source_panel, target_tag, panel_rect, x_rel, y_rel) -> resolve_drop match: OuterDock->dock_outer_preview_overlay, Dock->dock_drop_preview_overlay, Float/SnapBack->None (tint = dock_redock_preview_tint(Theme::default())). Imports dock_drop_preview_overlay/dock_outer_preview_overlay/dock_redock_preview_tint.

view.rs: view_main appends dock_outer_zone_highlight(zone) to the surface root when drop_preview.target == OUTER_DOCK_ZONE_TAG (same-window outer preview). Imports OUTER_DOCK_ZONE_TAG + dock_outer_zone_highlight.
diag.rs: redock_resolution(pane, target, x_rel, resolution) typed diag (reads a no-op drag off SPRAG_GUI_LOG); called in the redock_at arm.

Round 90.decision_summary: Round 90: add HEADLESS regression guards for the R87 drop-preview, correcting a testing-methodology error the user caught. When the user asked whether "preview is only live-verifiable" is normal, the honest answer is NO -- I had conflated two different things: (a) driving the mid-gesture DRAG via synthetic RPC (which IS limited -- scene/drag from_path can't resolve a header tag through the borderless main's chrome-inset wrap, the R85 artifact), and (b) verifying the preview RENDER, which is a pure function of the preview state and is fully headless-testable. Under pinion's scene-as-data philosophy, "only a human can verify" is a test gap, not an acceptable state, and it violated the R68 guard-faithfulness discipline (assert the rendered layout, not just the data path). Two guards added: (1) dock_drop_preview_hook_shows_for_a_dock_zone_none_for_own_slot -- calls the cross-window preview hook directly (the R87 addition the user reported missing) and asserts Some for a Dock zone / None for a SnapBack own-slot, through the same resolve_drop SSOT the redock arm applies (preview == result); (2) outer_drop_preview_state_appends_the_overlay_headlessly -- sets use_drop_preview to an OUTER_DOCK_ZONE_TAG target and asserts view_main appends the outer overlay (node count grows). Source finding: pinion's same-window highlights (per-panel dock_drop_zone_highlight, outer dock_outer_zone_highlight) are UNtagged, so the outer one is asserted by node-count delta; only the cross-window hook overlays carry DOCK_DROP_PREVIEW_TAG.
changes_bullets: main.rs tests: scene_node_count(scene) recursive helper; guard dock_drop_preview_hook_shows_for_a_dock_zone_none_for_own_slot (booted-topology owner; edge over another panel -> Some, own slot source==target SnapBack -> None); guard outer_drop_preview_state_appends_the_overlay_headlessly (render view_for_window("main") in the owner the use_drop_preview signal is set in -- Frame is unused by view_main; OUTER_DOCK_ZONE_TAG preview grows the node count vs the no-preview baseline). No production code change -- guards only.
verification_bullets: sprag-gui 68/0/0 (+2 guards) + clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean; rustfmt clean; cargo doc -D warnings (private items) clean. The two preview guards run headless (no GPU, no live drag) and pin the R87 preview render: the cross-window hook returns an overlay for a dock zone and nothing for a snap-back; the same-window outer overlay is appended when the outer-zone preview state is set. This is the regression fix for "only live-verifiable" -- a live human drag is now only the final visual confirm, not the regression guard.

The RPC-vs-live split stands -- driving the mid-gesture drag via scene/drag from_path is blocked by the borderless-main chrome-inset (R85 artifact), but the preview RENDER (the pure function of state) is guarded. Lesson: don't conflate "can't drive the gesture via RPC" with "can't verify the feature" -- verify the render as a pure function ([[query-the-wire-not-source]] sibling: test the deterministic render, not only the live gesture).

Round 91.decision_summary: Round 91: fix the STRUCTURAL flaw the user caught -- dragging the sole docked pane (which cannot float, tmux semantics) still showed a drag-image chip + drop-preview, because R87's refuse was at the wrong layer (a reducer-level silent swallow AFTER pinion's generic drag machinery already painted the affordance). The correct fix is to block the drag AT THE SOURCE via pinion R1172's per-panel DockPanelExternal::with_movable(false): begin_drag returns None for a non-movable panel, so no drag session, no chip, no preview. Wired dock::pane_is_movable(i) = !float_would_empty_the_dock(i) into with_movable in create_extra_externals; added a diag externals_rebuilt to read the factory's computed movable flags off SPRAG_GUI_LOG. HONEST OUTCOME: instrumentation proved the factory re-runs on float and computes movable=[false,true] correctly, BUT the live source-block does NOT take effect -- pinion's CoreShell::reconcile_externals early-returns when the tag set is unchanged (sprag's tags are constant, R70), DISCARDING the rebuilt external, so with_movable is create-time-only and the boot value (both movable) sticks. That is a pinion limitation -> filed PINION-PR42 (re-apply per-panel flags on the preserved node, or make them reactive). The with_movable wiring is kept as the correct forward seam (sprag change 0 when pinion delivers); until then the reducer/float gate keeps BEHAVIOR correct (the pane can't actually float/leave) while the chip/preview still wrongly shows.

Round 92.decision_summary: Round 92: adversarial SESSION REVIEW of the R77-R91 dock UX arc (the R52/R59/R61/R71/R76 pattern: 3 independent lenses + self cross-check), then remediation. Lenses: (A) SSOT/layering/north-star, (B) hacks/smells/DRY/dead-code, (C) test-guard faithfulness. VERDICT: ZERO must-fix BEHAVIORAL bugs. The structure is sound and verified: the "last docked pane can't float" decision is single-sourced (float_would_empty_the_dock, with pane_is_movable = its negation); the two dock authorities (windows-signal float authority vs use_dock_topology shape authority) stay orthogonal with the docked set DERIVED; the north-star is compile-enforced (sprag-host has no pinion-shell/widget-paint/vello dep; the three new WidgetView hooks live only in the GPU crate; no pixels painted in sprag); the reducer wire-faithfulness holds (exact scoped tags + payloads, real-state assertions); dock_drop_preview and the redock arm share the resolve_drop SSOT so preview==result. The defects were all in the SAME class the review was built to catch: DOC/NARRATION honesty + stale docs (R59/R76 class) — three docs overclaimed a live behavior that is not live (pane_is_movable's chip/preview "solved", the tear_off_redock_at test's live floater->main gesture, the module's placeholder-as-THE-model) and two module docs were stale about delivered pinion PRs (PR-35 height reflow, delivered R78; PR-34 collapse zone-redock, effectively delivered inside R1173). Plus one diag-cost smell and one centralization improvement. Notable: writing the C-3 collapse-redock guard SURFACED that pinion R1173's dock_panel_at_resolved_zone is total over an absent source leaf, so COLLAPSE now ALSO zone-honors a cross-window redock (the old "index-relative / PR-34 v1 bound" docs were stale) -- a real behavior correction the review found.

Round 95.decision_summary: Round 95: consume pinion PR-43 (delivered R1171/R1186/R1187, pinned R94 at c0fbac5f) so a torn-off pane window draws ONE strip -- controls-in-header. The floater's dock-panel header (already the drag surface + pane identity since R74/R1116) now also hosts the window controls: window_chrome(pane-{i}) -> None kills the redundant injected title bar, the new window_resizable hook (R1186) keeps the chrome-less window resizable (below-titlebar border, header owns the top), and view_window_controls (R1187) renders min/max/close in the header-trailing slot with the shell's WINDOW_CHROME_*_TAGs so try_chrome_press routes them exactly as chrome buttons (close = redock, R86 semantics preserved). Main window unchanged (chrome strip stays). Answers the user's R93 question ('why does a torn-off terminal need a window title? put min/max/X next to terminal-1') with the exact seam pinion built for it -- sprag is the second consumer after the editor. Live-verifying the buttons exposed a NEW introspection-drive parity gap: RPC scene/click bypasses try_chrome_press (winit-pointer-only), so window controls are observable but not RPC-drivable -> PINION-PR44 filed (with a secondary unsized-live-mirror finding); human mouse fully works.
changes_bullets: view.rs view_for_window floater arm: view_dock_panel -> view_dock_panel_with_actions with header_trailing = pinion R1187 view_window_controls (min/max/close glyph buttons), tags = shell WINDOW_CHROME_{MINIMIZE,MAXIMIZE,CLOSE}_TAG (binding supplies routing tags; widget-paint stays overlay-independent); font from DockPanelStyle.header_font_size_px.

main.rs window_chrome: a pane-{i} floater now returns None (was Some(default)) -- its dock-panel header IS its title bar (ONE strip); main unchanged (Some(default), client chrome). NEW WidgetView::window_resizable hook (pinion R1186): Some(true) for floaters so the chrome-less window keeps a client resize border (below-titlebar variant: header owns the top edge); main None = derive-from-chrome (unchanged full 8-dir border).
Close semantics preserved: floater close still routes window_close_requested -> redock (R86); the X now sits next to the tab label instead of a separate strip.

Round 99.decision_summary: Round 99: replace sprag-gui's ad-hoc SPRAG_GUI_LOG=1 boolean eprintln diagnostics with production-grade leveled `tracing` logging, adjustable by log level (user directive, now a standing project rule). diag.rs's typed events become `tracing` events with per-subsystem targets (sprag_gui::input / sprag_gui::dock) at audience-appropriate levels (per-key fan-out = trace, topology mutation / drop-zone verdict = debug, startup = info); main() installs a SPRAG_LOG EnvFilter subscriber (default warn, stderr, uptime timer) BEFORE pinion_shell::run() so it wins the idempotent try_init and sprag owns the env-var name + defaults (pinion's PINION_LOG init_tracing becomes the no-op fallback — same tracing substrate, one global subscriber). This uses the substrate pinion already blessed ("the permanent home for first-party diagnostics — no eprintln add/remove churn") instead of the hand-rolled boolean gate. Operators now dial verbosity per subsystem, e.g. SPRAG_LOG=sprag_gui::dock=trace.
changes_bullets: diag.rs: rewrote the SPRAG_GUI_LOG=1 boolean eprintln diag into leveled `tracing` events. Each typed fn (key_in/chord/dock_toggle/redock_resolution) now emits a `tracing` event with a per-subsystem target (`sprag_gui::input`, `sprag_gui::dock`) and structured fields instead of a formatted eprintln string; call sites (main.rs/input.rs/dock.rs) are unchanged.
Levels by audience: key_in + chord = trace! (per-key-event fan-out); dock_toggle + redock_resolution = debug! (topology mutation / drop-zone verdict). main() adds an info! startup line (pane count).

New diag::install(): a `tracing_subscriber::fmt` global subscriber env-filtered by SPRAG_LOG (default "warn"), stderr writer, uptime timer (process-relative stamp preserving the old ms-gap readability). Called FIRST in main() before pinion_shell::run() so it wins the idempotent try_init (pinion's PINION_LOG init_tracing becomes the no-op fallback) — sprag owns the env-var name + defaults.
Cargo: tracing + tracing-subscriber(env-filter) added as workspace deps (versions match pinion's, so the one global subscriber is shared) + wired into sprag-gui.
verification_bullets: cargo build -p sprag-gui clean; workspace tests 219/0; clippy -p sprag-gui --all-targets clean (fixed one doc-list-item lint); rustfmt clean; RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc clean.

LIVE (SPRAG_LOG=sprag_gui=debug): startup logged `INFO sprag_gui: sprag-gui starting panes=2` + a Ctrl+Shift+Enter undock logged `DEBUG sprag_gui::dock: dock_toggle pane=0 dir="undock" before=1 after=2`, both uptime-stamped; the trace-level key_in/chord were correctly filtered OUT at debug. DEFAULT level (no SPRAG_LOG) = 0 sprag_gui lines (quiet, warn floor). Level filtering confirmed both directions.
carry_forward_bullets: PROJECT RULE established (user directive): sprag logging is production-grade `tracing` with env-filter LEVEL control, NOT ad-hoc eprintln/boolean gates. Saved to memory (production-logging-tracing). Supersedes the R66 SPRAG_GUI_LOG=1 boolean diag.

Follows pinion's own principle (init_tracing doc: "the permanent home for first-party diagnostics — no eprintln add/remove churn"); sprag installs its subscriber first so it owns SPRAG_LOG + defaults while pinion's PINION_LOG init stays the fallback (both feed the same tracing substrate).
Future first-party diagnostics use tracing macros with a `sprag_gui::<subsystem>` target at the right level (lifecycle/state=info, per-event fan-out=trace/debug), never eprintln.
